name: Salvation by grace through faith
about: Saved by grace through faith in Christ, without works.

teachings.title: A new song of His great salvation
teachings.summary: Psalm 40 rejoices in God's deliverance from the miry pit of sin onto the rock Christ, showing that God never required sacrifices to save but only faith in His promises, which comes by hearing His word and calling on His name.
teachings.text:
After the somber and broken-hearted appeal of **Psalm 39**, **Psalm 40** gives us the rejoicing of those that trust in the Lord, and declares His power to all.

How wonderful is our patient waiting on the Lord, having called out His name for deliverance, to be rewarded by seeing Him turn towards us to save us in love!

He frees us from the miry pit of sin, He delivers us out of tribulation and temptations. He brings us from the shifting sands of doubt and fear, and sets us upon a rock. Our rock, Christ Jesus. The solid ground where He establishes our goings, and directs our paths. Praise Jesus for His great salvation!

We who are saved have a new song in our heart, the gospel which we preach, the good news of eternal life and forgiveness in Christ, *even praise unto our God: many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the LORD*.

*Blessed is that man that maketh the LORD his trust, and respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies.*

Is there any better news than this? Repenting from lies to trust in the Lord, and the blessings that we are given by His grace in exchange. Eternal life, His perfect word, His judgments. The Spirit of truth. The rejection of the proud. The deliverance from the evil of others. Made sons of God and joint-heirs with Jesus. Many are the wonderful works that our Lord God has done!

The tone of worship and blessings towards God in this prayer song of gratitude is as infectious as it is doctrinally rich.

The thoughts of the Lord towards us, that He even considered a wretch like me, the wonderful things He has for us cannot be numbered. There's not enough time or words in this life for us to declare all He has done for us.

All we can do is cry out, "Thank you!" And share this good news with others.

*Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required.*

The blood of bulls and goats never took away sin. It may have cleansed the flesh to be in the presence of God in the temple made with hands, but to enter into His presence forever, in the Temple of Heaven, all He has ever required was faith in His promises.

**Romans 10:17**
*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God*.

Have they not heard? The word of God has gone out to the world and not returned void. But those that harden their hearts, and stiffen their necks and refuse to obey the gospel of God.

As Jesus and the prophets taught:

**Matthew 13:13–16**
*Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand. And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive: For this people’s heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them. But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.*

God has blessed us with the conviction of the Spirit, that even in the miry pit, we heard Him, and see with our eyes the mighty God, being converted and healed. Calling upon the name of the Lord.

**Romans 10:13**
*For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.*

teachings.title: In His favour is life
teachings.summary: God's anger is for a moment but His favour, grace through Christ, is life, and the purpose of our salvation is to sing His praise forever.
teachings.text:
O LORD! In Psalm 30, David extolls the Lord for His gift of salvation, and calls all in the congregation to do the same.

God has lifted us up, heard us when we called upon His name, and healed us from our sin. We are brought up from the grave and shall never perish. Our souls will not see Hell. We shall not go down to the pit.

*Sing unto the LORD, O ye saints of his, and give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness.*

Rejoice! This verse makes me think of the Lord's supper. The thanksgiving and remembrance of Jesus' holiness.

**1 Corinthians 11:24**
*And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me.*

This communal act of thanksgiving and memorial - *For as often as ye eat this bread, and drink this cup, ye do shew the Lord's death till he come*. For this we should sing unto the Lord, extolling His mercy, forever.

*For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life*. The chastening of sons by the Lord is fleeting. But grace, the unmerited favor of God, is given to the world through His Son. And in His favor is life.

**Romans 6:23**
*For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.*

What a wonderful promise. How can we not sing for joy and give Him glory?

The comfort we have in Christ, knowing that *weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning*, knowing for certain that in our prosperity, in the gift of God, we shall not be moved. Our enemies shall not overcome us. We are made to stand on a sure foundation, the rock that is Christ. By His favor. By His grace.

We can trust that no matter what we face, even if we have angered God, that by turning to Him and crying unto Him, we have access to His grace through faith and the mediator of that faith, the man Christ Jesus.

The psalmist calls on God, reminding Him of His grace and mercy, the favor with which He has blessed us. And one of the purposes of our salvation, our healing, our getting saved, is that we will live forever to sing His praise.

The resurrection is sure.

Some will say the context of the Psalm is thanksgiving for not being killed by David's enemies, and triumphantly giving credit to God, but ultimately it is a song extolling the grace of God that those who trust in Him shall never perish.

*Hear, O LORD, and have mercy upon me: LORD, be thou my helper.* This is our prayer of salvation. Lord have mercy on me, a sinner. Knowing that God, Who cannot lie, has promised that all who call upon His name shall not perish, but be saved.

*Thou hast turned for me my mourning into dancing: thou hast put off my sackcloth, and girded me with gladness*...Jesus saves. Death has no sting for those in Christ. And while we may celebrate victory in this life, it is the victory of the cross that we should give thanks and praise, forever, because the purpose of God's sparing us, temporally or spiritually, is that we may sing His praise:

*To the end that my glory may sing praise to thee, and not be silent. O LORD my God, I will give thanks unto thee for ever.*

*To the end*, that is, the purpose of His salvation, our singing praise to God. Ultimately, that is what it is all about. Recognizing the glory and grace of a perfect and holy God. Amen

teachings.title: Only God can subdue the dragon
teachings.summary: Leviathan pictures Satan and sin, which man cannot subdue, bargain with or tame, so Job, like us, is restored only by God's grace and the blood of Christ, not by his own righteousness.
teachings.text:
In **Job 41**, God illustrates human inability to subdue the leviathan. No one can catch it like a small fish using a hook, line, or thorn through its gills. It will not plead for mercy or agree to serve as a captive. It cannot be tamed or confined like a pet bird for amusement. Its flesh is not suitable for food, and it cannot be caught and divided as spoils among merchants. Any hope of capturing it is vain; the mere sight of it overwhelms even brave men, causing them to faint. Attempting to lay a hand on it is futile—remember the battle and the impossibility of prevailing against such power.

If the leviathan is a picture (real or spiritually, or again, both) of Satan and of the sin of this world, isn't it a fitting analogy?

Man is helpless against sin on our own. We can't subdue it, reason with it, enter into a covenant to make peace with it, control it, enslave it, or truly make profit from it. It produces fire that burns all in its path, leaving behind it a trail that shines behind it.

Even air cannot slip between its scales. Its armor is impenetrable. Iron and brass are nothing to it. The mighty fall as it rears up.

Satan himself initiated the trial of Job, that the old serpent could accuse the man God described as perfect in his ways. And since the destruction of Job's life, his wealth, posterity and health, the Devil is noticeably absent afterwards.

There is a kind of closure to the story here, in the penultimate chapter, to see God describe a beast too fierce for man to handle, yet nothing to Him. Just as man is incapable of destroying sin and death and the fires of Hell, himself.

Job isn't restored by his own wisdom, his works, by proving his own righteousness before God. When the Lord offered Job to gird up his loins and confront Him, Job could only cover his mouth and sit in silence.

So, it is God who restores Job.

Only by God's grace do we find a way to overcome the world, death and Hell, by the blood of the atonement shed by Jesus, and everlasting glory by His life, risen in triumph.

Only God can subdue the dragon. Man is helpless against it.

teachings.title: How should a man be just with God?
teachings.summary: Job sees that no man is righteous before God and none can plead his own righteousness without a mediator, the man Christ Jesus to come.
teachings.text:
**Job 8** ended with Bildad the Shuite proclaiming that God is just to punish the unrighteous, and to bless the righteous; *Behold, God will not cast away a perfect man, neither will he help the evil doer*.

And here in chapter 9, Job again replies to the admonishment of a friend against him, saying sure, this is true, but then asking the key question; *How should a man be just with God?*

He says, if one were to argue with God, they couldn't win one of a thousand points of contention. That His wisdom and strength is greater than all others. Against the Almighty God, none could prosper. He moves the earth, destroys mountains, set the stars in constellations in the heavens, doing things that they cannot even imagine.

How can any man then be perfect before Him?

**Romans 3:10-12**
*As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God. They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.*

God is Spirit, unstoppable, His wrath undeniable. His judgment, impeccable.

Romans 1:20
*For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power*.

Job says, all the proud are humbled before Him and His fierce anger. So, what can Job even say to God in his sorrow and misery, to defend himself.

If God punishes the sinful, and no man is without sin, than any fate, even is extreme as what he's going through, is justified.

Because God is just.

So what could he say? How could he reason with God as to why he doesn't deserve what he's getting, when his friends all agree that sinners get punished while the righteous prosper, yet there are none righteous!?

If you were righteous, you could appeal to the judge your righteousness, but not before God. Why would he listen to a man? Does He answer to men, or men to Him?

Job bemoans his fate yet again, that he's broken and his wounds multiplied without a cause. That He won't allow job to die but filled him with bitterness. He could try to justify himself, but in doing so to a holy and perfect God would condemn him. Even his words to make known his righteousness, his filthy rags, would expose him as the sinner he is compared to God.

And so, Job comes to the conclusion that God destroys the perfect and the wicked alike. Bad things happen to good people, and bad people prosper. So it cannot be as Job's friends described. And if it's not, then all the lectures against him are hypocritical and vain.

He says for their sakes, he could stop complaining then try to comfort himself, because they're not comforting him. That no matter what he does they will not hold him innocent. They will say he deserves what he's getting. And good.

But he ask, if he truly is wicked then why is he bothering to explain himself? That even if he washed himself in purest water of melted snow, they would still hold him guilty.

But with God, there is no parity. There's no coming together and reasoning with the Lord, who knows all. There's no mediator of men between them *that may lay his hand upon us both,* he says.

His faith is in his Redeemer, and his Lord, but the only mediator between man and God, the man Christ Jesus, isn't a man yet. And so his fear of the Lord keeps him from appealing to the Lord in his tribulation. He can't even get comfort from his friends. That his situation is such, as he seeks to remain faithful and unwilling to curse God in his integrity, he doesn't know what he's supposed to do.

teachings.title: Laying the foundation with joy and weeping
teachings.summary: The shouts and weeping at the temple's foundation picture the joy over a new believer whose foundation is Christ, and the remembrance of God's mercy in older saints.
teachings.text:
**Ezra 3** continues the historic narrative being given, explaining how the circumstances of the author and his time came to be.

Here we flash back to 538–537 BC, and the Jews initial return under Cyrus’s decree and begin temple construction, laying the foundation for the Temple. This is roughly 17 years before Haggai and Zechariah, in 520BC. And before the full 70 years of captivity had expired.

The people celebrated and cheered the laying of the foundation and the beginning of their work. Doing the feasts and offerings as best they could, singing the songs of praise and worship. Blowing the trumpets.

But while the young people shouted for joy, the old men wept. They had seen the former glory and remembered what the first Temple looked like, and the Bible says the people couldn't tell the difference between the joy and weeping, it was so loud.

There is a parallel with Christians today. That as a believer comes to repentance, trusting in the Lord, there is great celebration, in Heaven, in the congregation, and in the heart of the person who has accepted the truth of Christ. This laying of the foundation of Christian life. Of the Temple of God. *For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ*.

*Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?*

When we sing *together by course in praising and giving thanks unto the Lord; because he is good, for his mercy endureth for ever*, toward the Israel of God.

But some weep, from regret or longing.

We cheer the new babe in Christ and perhaps remember when the foundation was laid in our hearts, and the joy that came. Maybe they weep to remember God's mercy on us when they were saved.

**Psalm 51:12**
*Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit*..

Still the shouts of joy and sadness are one voice. And the glory is God's.

teachings.title: Blessed are they that do his commandments
teachings.summary: Revelation 22:14 is Jesus' present exhortation to the saved, not a demand for works in eternity, where the curse is lifted.
teachings.text:
**Revelation 22:14**
*Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.*

This verse from the last chapter of the Bible, after John is wrapped up the revelation of Jesus Christ, pulled out of context to claim that in the new Heaven and new Earth we're going to need to do works to stay saved or something....wew. You know, after the resurrection after the glorified bodies after putting on incorruption after receiving that hope... Now we got to start doing works? LOL ok.

Context matters.

**Revelation 22:1-5**
*And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb. In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations. And there shall be no more curse: but the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him: And they shall see his face; and his name shall be in their foreheads. And there shall be no night there; and they need no candle, neither light of the sun; for the Lord God giveth them light: and they shall reign for ever and ever.*

This is the final prophecy for what it will be like in eternity. The curse is lifted. Every man and woman who was saved by faith will be healed and forever be with Christ, amen. What a glorious day.

Imagine trying to then add works, to place that curse of the law back upon us in perfection.

What a wicked thing.

Meanwhile, verses 10-16 are not describing the future. They are Jesus' message to the present. Encouraging we who are saved to keep His commandants, amen.

*I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches.*

People who wrest with scripture, using out of context verses and saying "it may not say this crazy thing, but it is implied!" are always undone by the word of God.

teachings.title: Turn yourselves and live
teachings.summary: Ezekiel 18's call to turn concerns national judgment and chastening, not eternal salvation, which cannot be lost.
teachings.text:
As for the use of this to teach "repent of your sins" for salvation, we understand that this is in the context of a nation being judged. While God's judgment is upon the wicked, and His mercy is upon those that walk in His ways, the wrath upon a people is based on their nation's sin. He will spare the righteous from His wrath. That's a promise.

**1 Thessalonians 5:9**
*For God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ*

**Romans 5:8-9**
*But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him*.

And here, in Ezekiel's day, God is reserving a righteous remnant that would survive, and thrive, under captivity.

The assumption is that if they are walking in His ways and keeping His precepts, they are doing so by faith. **Ezekiel 1**8 encourages that commitment. The need for it in saved people.

Note the warning to the backslidden is their death along with the unrighteous. But we know that judgment is just, but not eternal, because once saved always saved. God will take a backslidden Christian home in chastisement. So we should have a certain fearful looking over the shoulder when we seek to sin.

*Cast away from you all your transgressions, whereby ye have transgressed; and make you a new heart and a new spirit: for why will ye die, O house of Israel? For I have no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, saith the Lord God: wherefore turn yourselves, and live ye.*

teachings.title: The vine tree does no work
teachings.summary: The vine's wood does no work, just as believers are supported by the root, Christ, without works, while fruitless branches are burned.
teachings.text:
In **Ezekiel 15**, the word of the Lord came unto the prophet, and asks what is the vine tree, what good is it? It does no work. It isn't used for any task. It grows, it is only fit to be burned.

The Lord compares the inhabitants of Jerusalem to this vine, and that fire shall devour them like it becomes their trespasses.

Now, Jesus is the true vine, and the branches those people who are His and produce fruit, more saved people. And branches that don't are purged, the Bible says. Cut off. Fit to burn.

But it is interesting that the wood of the vine tree, when it is whole and growing, does no work. Just as we are supported by the root, which is Christ, without works.

teachings.title: Come, buy without money and without price
teachings.summary: Isaiah 55 echoes Jesus' call to come and drink freely, salvation by grace at no cost, and the word as seed that will not return void.
teachings.text:
Again, Isaiah is given the prophecy of Christ Jesus and the coming of the Holy One of Israel.

The chapter opens with a call to come and drink freely, to eat without money, without a price. Just as Jesus preaches throughout the gospels, especially **John 6** **and 7**.

**John 6:35**
*And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.*

**John 7:37**
*If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink.*

By grace, at no cost to us. Not the bread that satisfies not, paid for by our labors. But being full of His word, the goodness we delight in.

*Hear, and your soul shall live and I will make an everlasting covenant with you.* You can hear the voice of Jesus echoing to Isaiah.

A light to lighten the Gentiles, the nations that knew not.

*Seek ye the Lord while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near.*

The Lord has mercy on those who turns unto Him, for God will abundantly pardon our sins.

His word is the precious seed we bear as we share the gospel. And it will not return void. It will bring forth fruit, being seed to the sower and bread to the eater.

The picture of salvation by growing grain, just as Jesus preaches by parable. To the Lord, the increase. The harvest.

And we shall come rejoicing, bringing in the sheaves. Amen

teachings.title: Thou hast cast all my sins behind thy back
teachings.summary: Hezekiah praises God for salvation as a gift of grace, and those who refuse it have no hope, so today is the day to believe on Christ.
teachings.text:
Again, **Isaiah 3**8 retells **2 Kings 20**, and King Hezekiah's illness unto death, his calling upon the Lord to save him, and the grace of God to extend his life 15 years.

With the news from Isaiah, and the sign of the sun moving backwards in its path 10°, Hezekiah praises God.

 *O Lord, by these things men live, and in all these things is the life of my spirit: so wilt thou recover me, and make me to live. Behold, for peace I had great bitterness: but thou hast in love to my soul delivered it from the pit of corruption: for thou hast cast all my sins behind thy back. For the grave cannot praise thee, death can not celebrate thee: they that go down into the pit cannot hope for thy truth.*

Both praise for his healing, but more, the king praises God for His salvation. That men, including himself, had no love of peace. There is none good. All have fallen short of the glory of God.

But in His love, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. Salvation was offered, a gift given by grace, and our soul delivered from corruption. Casting all our sins behind us. Reconciled with a perfect and righteous God.

And those who forsake the gift, there is no hope for them. They that go down into the pit, into Hell, cannot hope for the Lord's truth.

Settle with the Lord in the way. Because by judgment, you'll be held to every sin. To the whole debt.

Now is the time. Today is the day. If you don't know for certain that you have eternal life, right now, that can never be lost, repent.

Believe on Christ Jesus. Become one of the living. The children of the Father. Sons of God.

Knowing: *The Lord was ready to save me: therefore we will sing my songs to the stringed instruments all the days of our life in the house of the Lord.*

Rejoice in His salvation. Amen

teachings.title: Precept upon precept on the cornerstone
teachings.summary: Jesus is the rejected stone made the head of the corner, the only foundation, and believers grow line upon line building works on Him that will be tried at judgment.
teachings.text:
Isaiah continues to speak the word of God, now against Israel and Judah. The princes who are drunk with wine and cannot rule justly. The priests and prophets, who err in vision and stumble in judgment. Vision often being the understanding and knowledge of the word of God, they preach vain things. Their tables full of vomit. Literally and spiritually.

*Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine? them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts*.

**Hebrews 5:13-14**
*For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe. But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.*

We learn the word, precept upon precept. Built like a wall, upon the cornerstone, level and plumb. Square and true. Line upon line. Here a little, there a little.

**Psalm 119:104**
*Through thy precepts I get understanding: therefore I hate every false way.*

Jesus is that cornerstone laid for us. The rock of our salvation upon which we stand. Like the wise man who built his home upon it.

**Psalm 118:22**
*The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.*

**Matthew 21:42**
*Jesus saith unto them, Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner: this is the Lord's doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes?*

**Acts 4:11**
*This is the stone which was set at nought of you builders, which is become the head of the corner.*

**1 Peter 2:7-8**
*Unto you therefore which believe he is precious: but unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner, And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed.*

There is no other foundation upon which man can built that doesn't come to naught, but Jesus. And we build up on that rock, precept by precept. Here a little, there a little. Until we are raised to judgment, and eternal life.

**Matthew 7:24**
*Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock*

**1 Corinthians 3:11-15**
*For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ. Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.*

Amen

teachings.title: Take with you words: Hosea's sinner's prayer
teachings.summary: Hosea's final appeal is a sinner's prayer: by confessing with our mouths we receive the free gift of eternal life, not by idols or our own works, and God heals our backsliding.
teachings.text:
Here, in the final chapter of **Hosea**, the Lord speaks through the prophet to make one final appeal of the gospel, that whosoever believes be saved.

He calls for Israel to repentance towards God, that they have fallen in their sin. (For all have fallen short)

*Take with you words, and turn to the Lord: say unto him, Take away all iniquity, and receive us graciously*, this is a sinner's prayer. (That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth...)

We are offered the free gift of eternal life in Christ, by the promise of a gracious God, Who takes away our sins, by the confession of our mouths. By the calves, the sin offering of our lips. Giving thanks to His name.

False gods shall not save us, nor the works of our hands. Note the double meaning here, both idols and literally the trust in our own works. For the Lord God is Father to the fatherless, in His mercy.

He heals our backsliding, loves us freely. We are no longer appointed to His wrath.

The Lord promises we will be watered as the lilies of the field. Taking root, spreading out like an olive tree. Growing as the vine.

And Ephraim, all Israel, will bring forth His fruit. After their kind.

*Who is wise, and he shall understand these things? prudent, and he shall know them? for the ways of the Lord are right, and the just shall walk in them: but the transgressors shall fall therein.*

He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

teachings.title: Let us walk in the Spirit
teachings.summary: Paul encourages believers to walk in the Spirit and bear its fruit, which shows the fruit is not automatic or outwardly obvious, rebuking fruit inspectors' hypocrisy.
teachings.text:
*This I say then, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh. For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh: and these are contrary the one to the other: so that ye cannot do the things that ye would. But if ye be led of the Spirit, ye are not under the law.*

After upbraiding the Galatians for being misled by Judaizers, and destroying the idea that salvation requires a form of sanctification of the flesh to be had, the Apostle goes on to encourage them to walk in the Spirit, that they can manifest the fruit of the Spirit:

 *But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law. And they that are Christ's have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts. If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit. Let us not be desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another*

Let us...If we...let us... Encouraging the brethren. If such fruit were naturally come by, and obvious to outside observation, it would not need to be encouraged. It wouldn't need to be something to strive for. And the provocation and envying, the accusing hypocrisy of fruit inspectors, the leaven of the Pharisses, wouldn't be being rebuked.

teachings.title: Easy believism accusers have fallen from grace
teachings.summary: Those who call grace easy believism and say struggling believers are not saved unless they turn from sin are self-righteous Pharisees adding works, while Christ died for us while we were sinners.
teachings.text:
Finally, if a hypocritical person like this comes to you saying that the gospel of grace and reconciliation in Christ Jesus is "easy believism" or "greasy grace," and that unless you turn from your sins and 'make Jesus the Lord of your life" you cannot be saved. That if you struggle with sin, backslide, or have an addiction that you cannot overcome in the flesh, that you must not be saved, understand that they are projecting.

They have fallen from grace. They are self-righteous. They are the leaven of the Pharisees which is hypocrisy. They are adding works to the free gift of salvation in order to shut up the kingdom of Heaven heaven from you, because it is shut up to them.

**Romans 5:6-11**
*For when we were yet without strength, in due time Christ died for the ungodly. For scarcely for a righteous man will one die: yet peradventure for a good man some would even dare to die. But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him. For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life. And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.*

Amen

teachings.title: This is all my salvation
teachings.summary: David's everlasting covenant shows salvation was by God's grace in Christ regardless of his or his house's unworthiness.
teachings.text:
David then says; *Although my house be not so with God; yet he hath made with me an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things, and sure: for this is all my salvation, and all my desire, although he make it not to grow.*

What a wonderful description of salvation! Although his house was not always right with God, his sin and the sin of his sons, still God had made a covenant with David in Jesus, the everlasting Kingdom to come of his seed. His salvation, and all David wanted. The Lord delivered regardless of David's worthiness and his own humble acknowledgement that it was undeserving, but for the grace of God.

David says that despite God delivering him and all he desired, all the good things that came from God, the Lord kept him from coveting more. Leaving him satisfied. We know that wasn't always true, but it wasn't of God when David coveted Bathsheba, but his sin was punished in this life, and David is looking at his eternal life to come, where his sin is remembered no more.

teachings.title: Saul's foolish vow added works to faith
teachings.summary: Jonathan's victory was won by faith, and Saul's commanded fast, adding works of righteousness and doctrines of men, only weakened the people and led them into sin.
teachings.text:
A long chapter for a quick story; Jonathan, the son of Saul, takes his armourbearer and goes up to spy out the garrison a Bethaven, and there, seeing a choke point between two rocks, senses an opportunity for the Lord to deliver his enemies to him.

Trusting in the Lord, Johnathan says if the Philistines call us down, we shall meet them because the Lord has delivered them to our hands. And by faith he allows them to see him, and of course they call him out. And Jonathan proceeds to smite them with his armourbearer behind, finishing them off. Twenty men fall at the first.

And the Philistines react in the camp and the vibrations and noise reach Saul who is sitting beneath a pomegranate tree, miles away.

Saul's watchmen tell him of the battle and he numbers his troops and realizes it is his son, faithful Jonathan.

First Saul asks for the ark of God, but the noise increased and so Saul says to the priest, "stay thy hand."

Where Jonathan went out by faith, Saul leaned on the ark, and it failed him. And so assembling his men, and the men disorderly came together, including the Hebrews among the Philistines and those in hiding, rallying to the battle Jonathan had begun.

Jonathan by faith showed leadership and courage that became infectious. And Saul, who had remained behind struggled to find the faith and leadership his son had displayed. Courage that brought out of hiding the fearful Israelites to attack the enemy camp.

Despite the success, Saul commanded the men not eat until evening, a fast he decided to decree after the victory had already begun. The Lord had already saved Israel that day. By faith, not of their own works. But Saul had commanded a fast.

And the men of Israel, exhausted obeyed. But Jonathan who hadn't heard his father's order, dipped his spear in honey that had by chance fallen on the ground, and ate it, the rush of it lighting up his eyes. Enlightened.

While the men all looked on with fear knowing the vow Saul had foolishly made, Jonathan points out how even the taste he had of it had enlightened him, say; *How much more, if haply the people had eaten freely to day of the spoil of their enemies which they found? for had there not been now a much greater slaughter among the Philistines?*

A picture of the Spirit that quickens those who eat freely of Christ, how much greater the victory had they gone by faith and Saul had not taught for commandments the doctrines of men.

And so they smote the Philistines and yet were faint with hunger, and so when they fell upon the spoils of sheep, ox and cow, they ate them straight away, with the blood.

And so Saul's foolish vow, adding works of righteousness to what was won by faith alone, led the men of Israel to sin.

teachings.title: Rahab and the scarlet thread
teachings.summary: Rahab the harlot was saved by her faith in God and placed in the line of Christ, her scarlet thread a picture of His blood, showing God can redeem anyone who holds the faith.
teachings.text:
And so we are here in **Joshua** chapter 2, and the newly anointed leader of the Hebrews is about to lead the people over the Jordan and into the promised land.

His first act is to send 2 spies to spy out the walled city of Jericho. This is similar to an earlier appearance of Joshua, in **Numbers 13**, where Moses sent 12 spies into the land, and 10 spies were bad and 2 were good.

Joshua and Caleb were the good men, who had faith in God to deliver the land to them. The 10 cast doubt and fear.

Not wishing a repeat, apparently, Joshua sends only 2, and these men make their way into Jericho by way of the home of the harlot, Rahab. There she lodges them and hides the spies when the king of Jericho sends out men to find them. The harlot hides the men upon her roof and sends the kings men on a fruitless search back towards Jordan.

She tells the Hebrew spies that she has done this because the whole land knows that the Lord God is with them, and are friegtened of them, considering the miracles of the Red Sea and the defeat of the other Canaanite kings. She has faith that the same Lord God will bring them victory in Jericho. The spies thank her, and she asks that they swear her family will be protected in their eventual siege of the city. The spies grant her an oath. That if she places the scarlet thread she had let them down on in her window, that all within her household will be saved.

Her faith in God to deliver the Israelites, and her faith in the promise of the spies, will lead to her salvation, as we will see in a few chapters. And the same faith serves as a picture of Christ. The scarlet thread, like the blood on the door frames on the first Passover. The same scarlet thread of the blood of Christ that runs throughout the Bible.

And Rahab is part of that bloodline of Christ Jesus, as we see during the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Matthew;

**Matthew 1:5-6**
*And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse; And Jesse begat David the king; and David the king begat Solomon of her that had been the wife of Urias*

The Greek spelling of 'Rachab,' is Rahab. She birthed Boaz of Judah, who eventually begets David, in the human lineage of Christ. A scarlet thread.

And she is saved by her faith, we know. Despite being a harlot. Despite her sinful life. She is redeemed, and honored with a mention in the Hall of Faith found in **Hebrews 11**, in the company of great Old Testament believers;

**Hebrews 11:31**
*By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace*.

She is also used by James, alongside Abraham, in his examples of those whose actions demonstrated to others the faith she had in her heart;

**James 2:25**
*Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way?*

Given as an example of faith by God, to show us that He may use anyone for His purpose, and redeem anyone who holds the faith.

teachings.title: An inheritance we did not build
teachings.summary: Like Israel given cities and wells they did not build, believers receive an incorruptible heavenly inheritance in Christ as a gift, to be remembered with humility.
teachings.text:
The Lord also reminds the Israelites that they are being given a gift that they did not work for. Cities they did not build. Wells they did not dig. Vineyards they did not plant.

*And it shall be, when the Lord thy God shall have brought thee into the land which he sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give thee great and goodly cities, which thou buildedst not, And houses full of all good things, which thou filledst not, and wells digged, which thou diggedst not, vineyards and olive trees, which thou plantedst not; when thou shalt have eaten and be full; Then beware lest thou forget the Lord, which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.*

This pertains to us, and the promise made to Abraham that was fulfilled in Christ Jesus. That it is to an inheritance uncorruptible, a heavenly Kingdom that contains many mansions. A land flowing with living waters and fruit of the tree of life.

We would do well to remember this, with humility and fear of the Lord. That we were bondmen, set free. That He delivered us and gave us an inheritance in a land we *buildest not*.

teachings.title: The Sabbath a picture of rest in Christ
teachings.summary: He teaches that the Sabbath pictures our rest in Jesus, that we contribute no works to salvation, and that those who add works damn themselves.
teachings.text:
*Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain: for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.*

Profaning His holy name, using it as a curse or to make a false vow, all take His name in vain. But worse are those who claim to be from God, using the name of the Lord to bring a false gospel or to justify evil.

*Keep the sabbath day to sanctify it, as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee. Six days thou shalt labour, and do all thy work: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, nor thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thine ox, nor thine ass, nor any of thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates; that thy manservant and thy maidservant may rest as well as thou*.

The Sabbath has always been a picture of Christ, and the rest we have in Jesus. And the prohibition against working on that day was to illustrate that we contribute nothing to our salvation except to honor His sacrifice by trusting on Him to justify us before God.

It is a gift of God, not of works, least any man should boast.

Again, there are no equivocations or rationalizations that can possibly justify those who add their works to God's plan of salvation, given us in Christ. They damn themselves just as assuredly as the man who gathered wood in the wilderness on the Sabbath. Salvation by grace through faith without works has been the Gospel from the beginning.

teachings.title: God does the work; we merely trust
teachings.summary: God would do all the work to bring Israel into the land if they only trusted Him, a picture of salvation as a free gift without our works.
teachings.text:
We should be reminded by these Old Testament stories that God was going to deliver all of the children of Israel to the promised land, that He would do all the work. Going out before them. They merely had to trust in Him and He would do the rest. The picture of individual salvation is the same.

Never let others tell you you need to do works of your own to be saved, that it isn't a free gift paid for by Jesus, that grace isn't grace. Never make your sins or tribulations and problems to be a cause not to trust God. Never let your shame or fear keep you from turning towards Him.

When you do, you will see your faith grow. You will witness miracles. You will be led of God to places you can't imagine, and be given the opportunity to do great things for the Lord. To harvest fruit more abundantly. To have your faith quiet other people's fears. To counter those who give a bad report with the peace that passes all understanding. Be bold in Christ.

teachings.title: Salvation first, then follow
teachings.summary: Israel was saved by the Passover blood before the sea, the law and the journey, showing salvation comes first and following God after.
teachings.text:
It is right and good to follow the Lord, moving to His commandments. And accepting His will for our lives.

But again, people conflate or confuse the order of things. The salvation out of sin of Egypt had already taken place, with the shedding of blood of the Passover lamb. The baptism of the waters of the sea followed. The understanding of the law given. The sanctification of the people. The continuous atonement with burnt offerings and blood of the sacrifices. The command to follow where God takes us after that. Being led into the promised land.

The order of things is given that there can be no misunderstanding. God is not the author of confusion. People want to add and mix things based on their own ideas, not the word of God.

teachings.title: The ledger of sin paid by Christ
teachings.summary: The law's recompense plus a fifth for every trespass shows we could never pay our debt to God, and our only hope is Christ's blood.
teachings.text:
Next is the law of recompense for trespasses against another. That when a man or woman commit any sin (which is transgression of the law), they trespass against the Lord, and if guilty, they must confess the trespass and pay the person it was against whatever it cost them in damages, plus 20% for their trouble. And if it could not be paid to the person, then paid to their kin. And without kin, brought to the priest and offered to the service of God that atonement may be made for them.

Note the recompense is due God, and for every sin. God demands payment plus the fifth, which when you consider the sins of man in a given day, if all were to be covered, even a righteous and godly man could be bankrupt by the end of a few days.

But the redemption is covered in Christ. God's recompense for our sin paid for by the blood of Jesus, a propitiation for our sin, atonement given that we may be justified in that reckoning.

The concept of the ledger and the debt incurred by sin is given that we may know we can never do enough to offset it. Our only hope is in Christ.

teachings.title: Access by faith into this grace
teachings.summary: We access God's grace, offered to all men, by faith as a free will choice, contrary to Calvinism, and salvation is a free gift without works.
teachings.text:
I wasn't going to take detours in this exercise of Dispensationalism in light of the book of Romans, but I cannot overlook the beauty of chapter 5 and the understanding that everything is in Christ Jesus; *By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God.*

Note this carefully. The Calvanist says the special boys chosen by God have access to faith by grace, but the Bible says the exact opposite. We access His grace, which abounds and is to all men, by faith. Just as Adam accessed death by the choice of sin, we access life in Jesus by the same free will choice.

*Therefore as by the offence of one judgment came upon all men to condemnation; even so by the righteousness of one, the free gift came upon all men unto the justification of life.*

Salvation is a free gift. Justification is of Christ. Offered to ALL MEN, by grace. Free. A gift, given without works, without being reckoned of debt. Without our having the glory. Without boasting, which is excluded.

*Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.*

This is the Gospel. And it is to all men. With the law or without. While we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

*That as sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.*

teachings.title: Justified by faith, offered to all men
teachings.summary: No fair reading of Romans yields faith plus works or salvation only for a chosen few, because Paul plainly concludes justified by faith and to all men.
teachings.text:
Again, it is impossible to read "*Therefore being justified by faith..."* and come away with "it's faith plus works."

Just as it's impossible to read *"to all men*" and say it's only for special boys, chosen because of their unique wonderfulness, "Hey, don't question a sovereign God. He just thinks I am super special and awesome."

God is not a respecter of persons.

It is impossible to say the Mosaic law did anything other than show man our own sinful nature, just as Adam transgressed under one commandment, then so too man transgressed all the more abundantly under the 600 or so contained in the law.

There is no fair reading of Romans that leads to these heresies. It is only by being a heretic first, and then searching for whatever scripture they can wrest with to torture into confirming their own vain imagination.

There are some who say the complex sentences and thoughts can be difficult for some to understand, but luckily for us God is not the author of confusion, and has Paul in the Spirit provide clear and concise summaries of each point as he concludes each argument.

"There is neither Jew nor Greek...."

"Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight..."

"To him that worketh not but believes..."

"Therefore being justified by faith..."

teachings.title: Just believe, but they had already chosen Egypt
teachings.summary: God promised the remnant deliverance if they only believed and stayed, but like many who ask what to do to be saved, they had already decided on their own way.
teachings.text:
Having been made desolate, spoiled. Many dead, more led away to captivity, and now, having the governor placed over them slain by one of their own, the remnant of Judah left in Jerusalem are desperate and full of fear. And in fear of destruction, they turn to Jeremiah, claiming to seek God's will for them in the calamity that's ensued.

They say they want God to show them the way wherein they may walk. The thing they may do, to escape destruction. They know the word of the Lord is with Jeremiah, who had for years and years preached the coming destruction, despite stocks and smiting, being jailed and left to die in mire. And all he prophesied has come to pass.

And they swear to the Lord that good or evil, they shall do as God tells them.

This is the way so many of us are, unsaved or saved. Those who come to inquire of the Lord, "What must we do to be saved?" Or those who are children of God, and yet not walking after His will.

They come to calamity, they see destruction ahead. They know they need to harken unto the word of God. They even will go to the godly to inquire, "What may we do?" swearing to obey. But in their hearts, they've already decided on Egypt; to sin.

These men of Judah are told to trust in the Lord. To stay in the land, to not fear Nebuchadnezzar. To trust the Lord, that He *is with you to save you, and deliver you from his hand*.

God promises them peace, mercy, to be returned to their own land. If they believe the word of God, they shall be saved. Note they didn't have to do anything other than believe that He would deliver them. That God repented of His wrath, if they simply obey His word. They didn't have to go anywhere. Do anything. Just believe.

But God knows the heart of man, and He knew they hadn't asked Jeremiah to hear the truth, but to be told what they wanted to hear. That it was ok to flee to Egypt.

That they should take it up on them to save themselves.

The Lord promises them that if they don't believe on Him that delivers the faithful, they will be destroyed. That in Egypt, they will die by the sword and famine and pestilence. That they would become an execration, a reproach, a curse. That people would use their fate as a warning to all those who do not obey the good news given by the word of God.

Unsaved people today will inquire of us, asking what they must do to be saved. And most will hear the gospel and refuse to obey it. They will seek their own works as justification. Or flee back to sin, as these Jews fled to Egypt, ignoring the warning of their destruction.

And some saved Christians, who believed the gospel and know the word of God is true, that He is faithful, will still fall into sin and in tribulation, refuse to standfast in the faith, but as the house of God, turn from Him disobeying His word, to their destruction.

As Peter asks us; If God will destroy those who are His, chastening every son He receives, if His judgment begins in His own house, against His people, what will He do to those who don't obey the Gospel?

teachings.title: Easy-believism and the strait gate
teachings.summary: Salvation by believing on Christ alone, mocked as easy-believism, is the strait gate few find, because pride, works and the false hope of repent-of-your-sins preachers keep men from simply trusting that Jesus paid it all.
teachings.text:
**John 3:16-18**
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.*

**Acts 16:30-31**
*And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved? And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.*

This is the Gospel of faith, taught throughout the Bible. But it is derisively called "easy-believism" by those seeking to bring another gospel of works and self-righteousness.

If believing the Gospel for salvation were "easy," then why do so many people struggle with trusting in Christ Jesus alone for their salvation? Why does every false religion reject this simple faith for works and penance?

**Matthew 7:13-14**
*Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.*

Believing on Christ alone for salvation is the narrow way. The strait gate. And there really are few who find it.

Pride and vanity and inability to trust the word of God keeps people from letting go and trusting by faith. They want reassurance that it "worked" before they can let go. They are carrying so much of a burden, and yoked by the law, that they cannot fit through that strait gate. Like a camel trying to pass through the eye of a needle. And so they seek a wider path to their own destruction.

Or they want to force their way through by exhibiting signs of deserving it through their own acts of righteousness, which the Bible calls filthy rags. Greasing the entrance by their own good intentions, so that they can accept that they "deserve" to enter. Not realizing none deserve it, but we are given entrance through Christ.

They want to know without trust, so that they may believe, and so they never can come to the knowledge of the truth. Because *faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen*. And without visible evidence, they doubt, and are given false hope from the "Repent-of-your-sins" types who claim that they may know they are saved if they do certain acts, and behave a certain way. But that false hope gives way when any weight is put upon it, because their standards are impossible to achieve in the flesh. It is impossible to pass through that gate carrying our own works, which are wood, hay and stubble, fit to be burned.

We don't begin to be sanctified until we are in the kingdom already. Until we have passed through that gate. Without faith, it is impossible to please God.

So don't be fooled. Salvation is easy, from a works standpoint because it doesn't require any effort from us to believe that Jesus paid it all. But it is hard from a human standpoint, letting go of all the burdens that keep us from passing through.

teachings.title: Carry no burden on the sabbath
teachings.summary: The command to carry no burden through the gates on the sabbath pictures salvation without works, the rest found in Christ.
teachings.text:
It feels like the prophet shifts gears, to give the word of God to the Jews in Jerusalem to remember the Sabbath. To carry no burdens through the gate to His city, but it is the same message. The Gospel of salvation without works. The rest found in Christ Jesus.

The burdens are works of righteousness that a man may store up, placing his hope in himself. In his ability to turn from sin, to turn his life around. His sin offering and incense, carried through the gates to join the assembly. But their hearts are far from Him because they are trusting in themselves. Their own works.

The burden of the works of the law, when salvation is by God's grace, a gift of God received by faith. Not of ourselves.

teachings.title: Obey my voice: the only dispensation is grace
teachings.summary: God's command to Israel was to believe His voice and then walk in His ways, the one dispensation of grace through faith in every age.
teachings.text:
It is a change of heart He seeks, repentance towards belief on Him. Not acts of religion, not vain works. But trusting in Him, and in love, doing right to others. Not oppressing the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow. Not shedding innocent blood. Nor walking after other gods.

God says; *For I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in that day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices: but this thing I commanded them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you.*

This is the Gospel of the Lord. Obey His voice. Believe His word, and He will be our God and we His people. And then to walk in His ways, obey His commandments, that it may be well with us. They are for our benefit. Salvation by faith, adoption to be His sons, sanctification to our benefit, that we may be holy because He is holy.

This is the only dispensation that there ever has been. The dispensation of grace offered by God through faith, unto adoption, and by love unto obedience of His commandments.

teachings.title: The temple and sacrifices could not save
teachings.summary: The temple and sacrifices were a gift to those already justified by faith, not the means of it, as Abraham was saved before circumcision.
teachings.text:
In this, God also wants those Jews who were going into the temple, to pay lip service to the ordinances and sacrifices, while not having the heart of a believer, that these acts cannot save them. No flesh is saved by works of the law. They were given as a means to understand the promised Christ. They were given after the promise that if they believed on the Lord, He'd be their God and they'd be His people.

Just as Abraham was saved by faith before circumcision. The blood of bulls and goats didn't save them.

And to remind them, God says he will destroy the temple that they are counting on to save them. Just as He previously destroyed Shiloh, the sight of the Tabernacle in the North, over run by Philistines and Assyrians, and laying in ruin during the days of Jeremiah.

The sacraments and the temple were a gift to those already justified by faith. Not the cause or means of that faith.

Faith cometh by hearing and hearing by the word of God. OT and NT.

And as we know, *God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets*...the word of God came upon those He sent. And the people did not harken unto them. None believe the report. And so, the judgment of God is just, being provoked to wrath by a stiff-necked and gainsaying people.

*Since the day that your fathers came forth out of the land of Egypt unto this day I have even sent unto you all my servants the prophets, daily rising up early and sending them: Yet they hearkened not unto me, nor inclined their ear, but hardened their neck: they did worse than their fathers.*

And so, God says the time is coming where the Temple itself and all the high places and altars to false gods they had set up, will be destroyed. Babylon is coming.

teachings.title: Israel saved by the blood before the law
teachings.summary: Israel was delivered from Egypt by faith in the passover blood before receiving the law, so those who demand turning from sin before believing reverse God's order.
teachings.text:
Now the salvation of the children of Israel from Egypt, that are freed from the yoke of bondage, came in faith on the promise of God. That by the blood of the Passover offering they are spared death. That by the waters they passed through, baptized into a new people and brought to a land promised them of God. Flowing with milk and honey, a land taken by those who failed to fear and serve the living God, but set about to establish their own righteousness. And then sanctified by the Lord to His purpose.

This historical and physical story is a picture of the spiritual, and the individual salvation of us who believe and are adopted by God as His people.

And so we should notice the order of things; salvation is front loaded and found only by faith. For the salvation of Israel from bondage and death came by faith alone, by the blood.

The Isralites in Egypt were not told to change their ways first. To become holy first. To repent of their sins and throw themselves before God crying for mercy because of how wicked they were.

God decided in His grace to offer them mercy if they believed Moses and Aaron, and trusted in the blood of the lamb.

And so all Israel was saved.

Then they were baptized together. Then they were given God's law. Then they were told to sanctify themselves, for their own good and to better serve God's will.

Those who place the giving of the law before the acceptance of faith are in error. Those telling others they must turn from their sins first before they can believe are entangling them in bondage. Placing the yoke upon those who should be set free.

teachings.title: Faith in Christ the only religion that is not a cult
teachings.summary: True faith is the only religion not held by coercion, since salvation is revealed and given at the start and everything after is by free will.
teachings.text:
Faith-based Christianity of those who believe the gospel and are saved by grace through faith, is the only religion that is not a cult. Because it is the only religion that is not held together by gnostic revelation, coercion, threat or manipulation. Everything from salvation, sanctification and discipleship, separating yourself to the Gospel, feeding the new man, walking in the spirit, everything is by free will.

We are given the highest enlightenment at the beginning. We are made sons of God. The ultimate mystery is revealed at our initiation. The truth of the gospel of Christ.

We are commanded to do things. To turn from sin, to be blameless that we may be better servants. So that we can share the gospel and give this truth to others in love. And to edify our brethren who are initiated into the election of grace.

Every other religion requires you to do these things or be cast out. Every other religion hides the ultimate prize. Every other religion requires you to adhere to their dogmas and traditions in order to maintain or attain salvation. They are cults.

Individual Bible believing New Testament churches may have standards that go beyond the basics as we are taught in the Bible. And if they require you to do them as a condition of attendance that's on you to accept or walk away from.

But the actual religion of God is entirely of free will. He might chastise us obviously and he might reward us to reinforce good works. But it's our choice everyday to pick up that cross. It's our choice everyday to kill the old man, and that choice is easier when you know for certain that you are saved. Amen

teachings.title: Wedding garment, not your own filthy rags
teachings.summary: Like the guest who refused the provided wedding garment, those who come in their own righteousness instead of Christ's will be cast into outer darkness.
teachings.text:
It's like, one of the Masters servants came to you and said "hey, I'm compelling you. You should come to this wedding feast." Or "hey you, person found you out here in the hedges and the highways, yes you random person, You got to come to my Master's son's wedding feast."

And you're going "listen, I'd love to come but I don't have any wedding clothes. Let me go make my own and I'll be right along."

And the servant is like, " No dude, Master has it covered. He's got a wedding outfit for you. Just come on."

And dudes like "Nah bro, I wear my own clothes. Thanks!"

And then you show up in your own filthy rags, and everybody else is in white linens.

The Master is going to say "hey throw that bum out! Cast him into outer darkness where there is wailing and gnashing of teeth and stuff."

Ya feel me, special boys?

teachings.title: God's glory revealed in our salvation
teachings.summary: God's glory is shown in salvation as a free gift of grace without works, so all who add works rob God of His glory.
teachings.text:
God's glory is revealed in our atonement by the blood and obedience of Christ. His mercy and grace are given witness. And so too here, as Moses consecrated Aaron and his sons into the holy priesthood, we see it witnessed, *that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory,*

**Exodus 33:17-2**0
*And the Lord said unto Moses, I will do this thing also that thou hast spoken: for thou hast found grace in my sight, and I know thee by name.*

*And he said, I beseech thee, shew me thy glory.*

*And he said, I will make all my goodness pass before thee, and I will proclaim the name of the Lord before thee; and will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will shew mercy on whom I will shew mercy.*

**Ephesians 2:4-10**
*But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us, Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ, (by grace ye are saved;) And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus: That in the ages to come he might shew the exceeding riches of his grace in his kindness toward us through Christ Jesus. For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.*

**Hebrews 1:3**
*Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;*

Just as we see God's glory revealed in wrath against the unrighteous, it is truly revealed in our salvation from that wrath, the good news of His free gift. In His grace and love.

This is why salvation is so simple that a child can understand it. This is why it is without works, that no man can boast of having deserved it. That all the glory be given God. This is why we who believe on Him that is faithful and true may know we have eternal life. That we are sealed unto redemption by His Spirit. That He testifies within us. That we may have that blessed assurance. Eternally adopted sons and daughters of God.

To show His glory.

And all those who seek to establish their own righteousness, who deny the eternal gift, who make grace into some sort of rewards system in a game, rather than the gift of God given in the blood of His only begotten Son, seek to rob God of His glory. It is blasphemy.

teachings.title: A zeal of God, but not according to knowledge
teachings.summary: Like Israel, zealous Catholics, Orthodox, Lordshippers and repent-of-sins preachers set up their own righteousness, but Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to believers.
teachings.text:
Following the end of the argument regarding Israel after the flesh and the utter rejection of the idea that they are saved by their kinship to Abraham in chapter 9, Paul begins chapter 10 of Romans by lamenting this sad fact; that his own people, Israel after the flesh have shut themselves out of the kingdom by seeking their own righteousness by works of the law rather than the righteousness of God by faith.

*Brethren, my heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved. For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.*

This same prayer and sad refrain, a testimony of ignorant zeal that is preventing those trusting in their works from obeying the law of faith, could apply to so many zealous Catholics and Orthodox, Lordshippers and Repent-of-your-sins types. Those who place their works, their turning from sin, pursuit of their own righteousness to be made worthy, rather than the humility to understand that none are righteous, that they may obtain God's grace and mercy through faith. They have a zeal for God, but go about to set up their own righteousness to their destruction. Just like Israel after the flesh.

*For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.*

They lack the understanding that by the end of the law for righteousness, actually establishes the law. **Romans 3**:

*Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yea, we establish the law.*

God's judgment reveals His holy righteousness through His mercy and His wrath. His law is the instrument by which we understand it, and our failings and the need for salvation by grace through faith. And by submission to the righteousness of God, we become able to truly fulfill the law. Without the spectre of death and hell, but rather with charity and love through faith.

teachings.title: They stumbled at that stumblingstone
teachings.summary: Gentiles attained righteousness by faith while Israel failed by seeking it through works, which is Paul's argument in Romans 9, not Calvinism.
teachings.text:
*What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory, Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?*

As the prophets spake, moved by the Spirit, God promised to bring men from all nations to be His. And as the prophets warned the Jews, that except for the seed, being Jesus, He would have destroyed Israel sooner, they would have been as Sodom. But being fitted to the purpose, He showed mercy, until establishing Jesus in Zion, a sure foundation for the believers, Jew and Gentile, but for the unbelieving Jews, a stumblingblock. A rock of offense.

And this is the argument Paul is making. It isn't about calvanism or Jews after the flesh, it is about Christ. Whatever twisted doctrines can be wrung out of Romans 9, the context is clear:

*What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, which followed not after righteousness, have attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith. But Israel, which followed after the law of righteousness, hath not attained to the law of righteousness. Wherefore? Because they sought it not by faith, but as it were by the works of the law. For they stumbled at that stumblingstone*.

Gentiles, through Christ have found righteousness. Jews, through the law, death. Why? Because they sought their own righteousness through works, rather than seek the imputed righteousness of Jesus, by faith.

It is the same argument Paul has been making since chapter 1.

We are saved by faith. It is God's righteousness, not our own. It is for His glory, not ours. Boasting is excluded. We are but clay to be shaped. The Creator is greater than the creation.

teachings.title: Righteousness by faith, not circumcision
teachings.summary: Abraham was counted righteous by faith before circumcision, so no rite, baptism, or work is required for salvation, and the inheritance is by faith in Christ, not by fleshly descent as Zionism and dispensationalism claim.
teachings.text:
So this is the promise made by God that if we believe on the Son, we are saved by His grace. Our sins forgiven. No sin even being imputed upon us. Whether we work or not, because work is debt not grace.

Paul continues using Abraham's example;

*Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness. How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.*

Abraham did not receive the ordinance of circumcision until decades after his believing God's promise, and being saved by that faith. He was blessed with the accounting of righteousness when he did not know circumcision. So this promise, predating this rite of the Jews, means it does not only apply to the circumcised, but also to the uncircumcised. And so the promise of grace doesn't require circumcision, but faith alone.

This point is both specific to the issue of circumcision being introduced by the Judaizers in Paul's day, but also generally speaking, that there is no rite or ordinance that is required for salvation. Not baptism. Not any ritual or keeping of tradition. No works of the law.

*And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also*.

Abraham as the father of all who believe, the circumcision of the spirit, the generation of believers are partakers of the promise, that the righteousness of God is imputed upon us in faith.

*For the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, was not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith. For if they which are of the law be heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of none effect: Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression.*

The promise of God that Abraham believed was that through his faith, he would be made father to many nations, and inherit the kingdom of God. This promise was made possible in Christ.

**Galatians 3:16**
*Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ*.

Unbelieving Jews felt they were owed the kingdom by God for being Abraham's seed under the law. That the inheritance was by blood, and the promise made to them after the flesh, and not in the spirit.

This is the basis for Zionism and the false doctrine of dispensationalism.

But the Bible teaches the exact opposite. There is no difference between Jew and Gentile. All are under sin. It is by faith only that we are made heirs. That the seed of the promise is Christ manifest in the flesh.

**Matthew 3:9**
*And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.*

It is not an inheritance by the law but by faith. Like Esua and Jacob, the inheritance went to the younger. It was taken from the elder, who with tears sought repentance from God, but none was found.

**Luke 13:25-30**
*When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are: Then shall ye begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets. But he shall say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity. There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrust out. And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God. And, behold, there are last which shall be first, and there are first which shall be last.*

teachings.title: To him that worketh not
teachings.summary: Anyone who makes salvation or keeping it depend on works claims God owes them and lacks the faith without which it is impossible to please God.
teachings.text:
*Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt. But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.*

But to him that worketh not, but believes, his faith is counted for righteousness just as Abraham's. Just as all who believe. Works has nothing to do with salvation. God doesn't owe us salvation.

Our works, no matter how good we think they are, can never offset our sin, and the wages thereof.

When someone says their salvation or their ability to stay saved is contingent on their works, they are saying they are good enough to please God. That they are owed salvation. That the glory is theirs. That their boastings before God are justified. That they don't need grace.

**Hebrews 11:6**
*But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.*

Their lack of faith in Christ to be the propitiation for our sin, the sole sacrifice pleasing and acceptable to God, means their works are dead. They have no grace and no works. They are incapable of pleasing God.

teachings.title: Abraham the father of us all
teachings.summary: The law works wrath, so the promise comes by faith through grace, making Abraham the father of all who believe, and the Jew has no claim to him outside faith.
teachings.text:
*Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression. Therefore it is of faith, that it might be by grace; to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham; who is the father of us all, (As it is written, I have made thee a father of many nations,) before him whom he believed, even God, who quickeneth the dead, and calleth those things which be not as though they were.*

Because the law brings wrath, because we are all under sin, it isn't by the law we are saved. It is impossible for all have sinned.

As James writes in the parts of his epistles ignored-by-works salvationists;

*For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.*

Remember, there are none righteous. Knowledge of the law brings wrath. But faith, the grace of God.

We access His mercy and forgiveness through faith alone. Plus nothing, minus nothing.

And in grace we receive the promise given Abraham, and count as his seed in the spirit. Adopted into the kingdom of God. Made sons of God. Abraham is the father of us all who believe.

 *(As it is written, I have made thee a father of many nations,) before him whom he believed, even God, who quickeneth the dead, and calleth those things which be not as though they were.*

God, who can see all things, the future which is not to us, and yet it appears as it were to God, who quickens the dead, who breathes life into our dead spirit, and who made this eternal promise to all who believe.

The Jew has no claim to Abraham, outside of faith. None. And to none of the promises made, for they all are fulfilled in Christ.
