If it feels like I am beating a dead horse, understand that it is God's word that stresses this over and over again, because it is the Gospel, the good news, that is the entire point of scripture. To bring us into the promise through faith and the imputed righteousness of God.

teachings.title: The gospel of grace in every age
teachings.summary: God's grace through faith was given in every age from Adam and preached by the prophets, and the Judaizers' works gospel persecuted it.
teachings.text:
So, to review, Paul has established the truth of God, the need for both Jew and Gentile to be saved. That all are dead in sin.

Now, recall the larger context of these epistles, established in **Acts 15**;

*But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses*.

These Judaizers were the main impetus for the epistles to the various churches by the apostles, to keep the newly regenerate Jews and Gentiles, babes in Christ, from being taken in by the false teachings of a works based salvation.

Now the grace of God was established with Adam, and every just man from Seth on called upon the name of the Lord to be saved. His grace was given in faith to all ages, and every prophet spoke of His longsuffering and salvation given to those who hear His word and believe.

In **Hebrews 11**, Paul gives a recitation of the more famous OT saints, saved by faith alone, after establishing what faith is.

*Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen. For by it the elders obtained a good report. Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear.*

The Gospel of grace caused the Jews to persecute Christians from city to city, even as they sought to creep into houses and corrupt them.

The Gospel of grace was preached by the prophets, seeking to turn Israel to repentance, and they were murdered for it.

As Jesus preached against the Jews in **Matthew 23**;

*Upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.*

teachings.title: Justified by faith without the deeds of the law
teachings.summary: The law shows all guilty so no flesh is justified by works, but God's righteousness is given freely by faith in Christ's propitiation, which establishes the law.
teachings.text:
And so, going back to Romans 3, having the full context of things, and an understanding of the conflict between these two visions; God's revelation of His righteousness, and the filthy rags of man's, we proceed.

*Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God. Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.*

Now we know. Everyone under the law should know that they all break the law. That all the world is guilty before God. That is the purpose of the law, to serve to humble us and reveal the holiness of God, that we may come to call upon His name to be saved.

(If a man were perfect under the law, they would be saved, but the exceeding holiness that is God, only the Son could achieve this in the flesh)

Therefore by the deeds, the doing, the works, none shall be saved.

It is impossible for man to work their way to Heaven. We cannot attain the righteousness of God.

And so what does this mean for us? Where is the good news? How can we attain righteousness if not by our works?

*But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets; Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.*

Read that again. And again.

Jesus Christ is the propitiation, that is a sacrifice that is wholly pleasing to God, that is the blood of Christ serves to impart His righteousness to us, by faith, to show us the righteousness of God in our forgiveness. We are justified freely by His grace. Even the righteousness of God, **that is by faith**, upon **all them that believe**.

That's the good news. This is the Gospel. This is the reason Romans is used to evangelize, because it is the clearest and most succinct summary of the Gospel.

All have sinned.
All deserve death.
Jews under the law. Gentiles without the law.
But God's grace is such that all who believe that His Son, Christ Jesus, the lamb without blemish, was given to be the propitiation for our sin, and that grace is given freely to all who believe.

*Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith.*

This is the end of the argument. There is no one who reads this and says "yeah, but you have to do works" who is seeking truth. They are blind in their own pride.

*Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.*

Read that again. Say it out loud. Three chapters of building argument against the judaizers, the works-based false gospel. The workers of iniquity.

*Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.*

Furthermore*:*

*Is he the God of the Jews only? is he not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also: Seeing it is one God, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.*
*Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yea, we establish the law.*

By understanding that salvation comes only by faith, we actually establish the law. By believing God's word, by placing our trust in the sacrifice of Jesus, that in His blood we are washed clean, forgiven of sins, we then understand the nature and purpose of the law, and are free to become doers of the law. To seek to obtain the holiness of God out of love.

To be holy because He is holy.

To reveal His righteousness to the world by our forgiveness in His grace.

teachings.title: The sabbath and the free will offering
teachings.summary: The sabbath pictured salvation by faith alone, so working on it meant trusting one's own works, and the free will offering pictures coming to Christ of our own free will.
teachings.text:
Quick one today. It is mostly a recap but two points; One, the sabbath is an ordinance pointing to Jesus, a memorial for generations to those Hebrews who believed God, and the salvation He offers as a free gift, and  comes by faith alone, not of works we do. That is why someone who worked on the Sabbath was put to death. They trusted their own works.

Second, note the free will offering to God of the children of Israel. Again, we come to Christ of our own free will, answering the call of God. Just as they did, and similarly we build up the temple of our bodies, a temple for the Spirit of God. Amen.

teachings.title: The sabbath, a picture of rest in Christ
teachings.summary: The sabbath pictures resting in Christ's finished work, so salvation is by faith alone, and keeping the seventh-day sabbath to be saved, as Seventh-day Adventists do, is judaized bondage while Christians gather on the Lord's day.
teachings.text:
**Mark 2:28**
*Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.*

**Matthew 11:28-30**
*Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.*

Chapter 31 provides an additional teaching on the sabbath, God instructs Moses to tell the people they are not to work on the last day of the week, least they be cut off and put to death. That the sabbath is a day of rest to memorialize His perpetual covenant, that it is by faith in the Lord that sanctifies us.

It is a fitting picture of Christ, in whom we are called to rest on His perfect work for salvation. That salvation is by faith alone, not of works. And if you reach the end and are trusting in your works rather than the sabbath God provided, you're perishing. You will be cast out and put to death, which is Hell.

People struggling with the idea that our works do not save us don't understand how the Sabbath is a memorial for the covenant of Christ. That we are free of the yoke of the law in regards to righteousness, because by the blood of Christ God will not impute sin to those that are saved when we are called to the Kingdom. They miss the point of the 3 sabbaths in a row between Passover and Easter Sunday, the first day of the week. That no works of the law shall save us. Jesus did it all.

7th Day Adventists and others under the yoke of the law keep the old testament sabbath, the last day of the week, in order to be saved. It is judaized nonsense.

Christians celebrate and gather on the first day of the week, the Lord's day, in remembrance of His resurrection and the establishment of the new testament. As a memorial throughout our generations that we may know He is the Lord that sanctifies us.

**Galatians 5:1**
*Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.*

teachings.title: Eating in His presence is not believing on Him
teachings.summary: Proximity to Christ, church attendance, family or works done in His name cannot save; only faith alone receives His imputed righteousness, as the wedding parables teach.
teachings.text:
Continuing a theme from **Luke 12** that I touched on [last night](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/9465), where Jesus is preaching the Kingdom of Heaven, and specifically addressing those who would not believe, mostly among the Pharisees, as a way of contrast that the other people may see the chief among them's error, and come to repent towards God.

Here, He has gone to supper bidden by a Pharisee, and sat among them on a sabbath, the Bible says, that they watched Him. Observing Jesus, looking to tempt Him as they've been. Looking to find fault. Some undoubtedly seeking status on f having supper with Him, as His ministry had grown. Looking for shared glory by proximity.

It reminds us of Jesus having said in chapter 12: *Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are: Then shall ye begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets. But he shall say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.*

And here we see them eating with Christ, just as He said.

The point is in the judgment, being in proximity to Christ isn't the same as believing on Christ. Doing works in His name, eating supper, His work done in your streets, in your church or even calling Him Lord, isn't sufficient to be saved.

To receive the imputed righteousness of Jesus. To be washed clean in His blood. That comes by faith alone, coming to understand that you are a sinner deserving death and Hell, and accepting the free gift of grace, forgiveness and reconciliation.

In the parable of the 10 virgins, waiting for the bridegroom that they may attend his wedding feast, Jesus says that some had oil prepared in their lamps, and when he arrived, went out and were taken into the feast. The rest, having no oil themselves asked for some of the other's, but they could not share. You can't be saved by being the son or daughter of a saved Christian. You cannot be made righteous by being the spouse of a believer. You can't be saved by going to a Christian church, partaking in the Lord's supper, or by trying to show up at the wedding feast in your own attire, clothes in the filthy rags of your own righteousness.

That's what all these parables about weddings and being cast out into outer darkness, with wailing and gnashing of teeth, it's what all these are teaching.

After healing a man with edema, there among the Pharisees on the sabbath, Jesus again puts the hypocritical men on the spot. They seek to hold the letter of the law against Him, while the spirit of it is revealed in the exceptions given to help a neighbor or even an enemy.

teachings.title: Strait is the gate, not difficult
teachings.summary: The strait gate is the one narrow way through Christ, and modern versions that make it difficult teach a hard salvation of works.
teachings.text:
Now Jesus has begun to make His way towards Jerusalem. His fate awaiting there, and He continues His mission, giving the Gospel to the poor that they may be redeemed.

A person asks if few will be saved, Jesus replies that we must enter in the strait gate, the narrow path, through Him. That many seek the kingdom but by the way that seems easy.

Similar passage to **Matthew 7:13-14**:
*Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.*

Modern false translations change the narrowness of the gate, the one path to salvation, to "difficult," teaching that salvation is hard and of works. But in the abbreviated telling in Luke the meaning is reinforced. Jesus is desperately trying to reach people with the truth, that they may turn towards God and be saved. The kingdom is nigh. Repent.

*When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are: Then shall ye begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets. But he shall say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.*

Another parable warning then not to be shut out. Not to be like the virgins who didn't keep oil in their lamps, and when the bridegroom returned were shut out of the wedding feast. Like the wicked servant who abused his station while the master was away, only to be found out by the Lord's unexpected return. Not to be caught unawares like a thief coming in the night, but to be watchful and ready. Jesus preaches hellfire and brimstone. The destruction that awaits all men who do not come to believe.

*There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrust out.*

teachings.title: Thy faith hath saved thee: a proof text
teachings.summary: Jesus' own words to the sinful woman prove salvation by faith alone, her love following her forgiveness, while the self-righteous Pharisee could not be saved.
teachings.text:
BTW there is the proof text from Jesus own mouth, red-lettered, the woman who is a great sinner is saved by faith alone.

That faith in Christ, her salvation, means she is forgiven her debt, and she shows great love and gratitude in return. He didn't say your works have saved you. Jesus flat out says her love for Him is due to her having been forgiven already. She isn't saved because she showed Him love and hospitality, with humility and sorrow for the sins she's done. Her faith saved her. The love she showed Him followed.

In contrast, Simon the Pharisee, who believed he was righteous by his works, his keeping the vain traditions and ceremony of men, along with the letter of the law, couldn't come to be saved, lacking the faith. Despite owing little, he couldn't see the Christ, the redeemer sitting in his own house. His judgment, his wisdom, justified by its children. Revealed by its fruits, and found wanting.

teachings.title: Adding Works Crucifies Christ Afresh
teachings.summary: Those who add their own works to Christ's sacrifice deny the Lord that bought them, deny His preserved word, and risk a hardened heart.
teachings.text:
Everyone who claims to be a Christian but denies the truth of the Gospel, adds their own works to their righteousness, refusing to accept that Christ's death was the propitiation for our sin, crucifies Jesus afresh and puts Him to an open shame. They deny the Lord that bought them.

And, inevitably, these same people who are perishing will deny the word of God is perfect. Inspired. Preserved. Casting doubt on the testimony of God the Father and refuse the call of the Son who was lifted up on the cross. And so they have no part of the better testament. And the rebuke of the Holy Spirit is upon them until such a time where their hardened heart is made permanent. In death or reprobation. And they damn themselves.

teachings.title: Works Without Faith Are Dead
teachings.summary: Works done to earn salvation are self-righteous filthy rags, and only the blood of the Lamb can reconcile us to God.
teachings.text:
Works without faith are dead, being vanity. They're useless. They are acts of self-righteousness, done selfishly on the hope that it will purchase indulgence for sin and avoid the fires of Hell. To offset the wages of sin which is death.

You cannot do good unto others when your motivation is earning salvation from the fires of Hell. The Bible says our works of righteousness are as filthy rags. They're wood, hay and stubble They earn no reward. They are burned up. For they can never offset the price of our transgressions. Only the blood of the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world can reconcile us with God. Only the perfect work of Jesus Christ can redeem us.

teachings.title: Ceasing from Our Own Works
teachings.summary: Entering God's rest means ceasing from our own works, since adding works shows unbelief in His finished work; Christ is our Sabbath.
teachings.text:
Continuing to reason with man, Paul writes that if it were only pertaining to the Exodus, and the offer of the promised land, if that was His rest given by a Jesus, then why would he say through David (again acknowledging who the real author of scripture is), that He would mention another day. And so, concludes there remains another day of rest for the people of God. Those who believe. That the picture of Exodus wasn't the fulfilment of Genesis. Jesus Christ is.

And entering in to God's rest, we end our own work, because it is God's rest, not our own, and His labor, not our own, and His work has been finished since the foundation of the world.

*For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.*

Using our own works to enter into His rest is a sign of unbelief that He did it all. Like Moses striking the rock twice for water. Like the Hebrews and mixed multitudes turning to the golden calf. Unbelief in God's word kept them from the promise.

But we are saved by the blood of the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world. We rest in His work, not our own. We enter into rest by faith. Belief. And having entered into the promise by faith, not work, we are in the Sabbath of Christ. Again a picture of salvation without works.

teachings.title: Watch and Keep Thy Garments
teachings.summary: Christ comes as a thief only to the unwatchful, and anyone can know today they are saved by faith alone in His finished work.
teachings.text:
*Behold, I come as a thief. Blessed is he that watcheth, and keepeth his garments, lest he walk naked, and they see his shame.*

In the midst of the narrative Jesus reminds us of His oft repeated warning that to those who aren't watchful, who aren't sober, who aren't in the word and feeding the new man, but are in the world and feeding the old, he will come unexpectedly as a thief. But we are to watch and to know the signs and not be caught unaware. Not caught naked and ashamed, but clothed in the blood of the lamb. Dressed in white linen wedding garments, given to all who believe and overcome in Jesus. Who have the testimony of Christ.

Make sure you are not walking naked. Make certain you aren't appointed to wrath. The Bible says you can know you are saved today, by faith alone in the perfect works of Christ Jesus. A free gift, given by the grace and mercy of the living God. Justification by the blood. Jesus death as an atonement for our sin. And His resurrection the promise of God's word kept.

If you have not received the free gift of salvation or aren't certain that you will be with the saints in Heaven on the glorious day of the Lord's return, please take a moment to listen to this message; the Bible way to Heaven.

For faith comes by hearing and hearing by the word of God.

teachings.title: Abraham believed God and was counted righteous
teachings.summary: Like Abraham, whose belief in God's promise was imputed to him for righteousness, salvation has always been by hearing and believing God's word, by faith alone and not by works.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 11:8**
*By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.*

**James 2:23**
 *And the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.*

**2 Chronicles 20:7**
*Art not thou our God, who didst drive out the inhabitants of this land before thy people Israel, and gavest it to the seed of Abraham thy friend for ever?*

Abraham believed. This is the verb form of faith, the noun, the thing Abraham had. He believed having faith in God's word. His promise. And that faith was imputed upon him for righteousness and he was called *the friend of God.*

If we believe, an action, if we have faith, the evidence of things unseen, a thing to possess, in the word of God, His promises, His testimony, we have His righteousness imputed on us. Projected upon us. Not our own righteousness. Not our works. But our faith, which comes from believing, which comes from the word of God.

O, to be called the friend of God for our faith!

Salvation has always been by hearing the word of God, believing it, which gives us faith to call upon the name of the Lord, for which God grants us His grace.

 Salvation is by faith alone. Yesterday, today and forever, amen.

teachings.title: Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord
teachings.summary: Noah was saved by grace through faith like every believer, the flood picturing Christ's death, burial and resurrection, and the giants were men.
teachings.text:
Here we arrive at the story of Noah, the flood and the destruction of man. Again, as we studied yesterday, only a short while, epochally speaking, after creation.

And as I pointed out in yesterday's study, the story of the patriarchs from Adam to Noah is the pattern of salvation given to us by God. Here, Noah by faith builds the Ark, obeying God, and is saved from destruction, the earth cleansed of it's wickedness in a global baptism, itself a picture of the death, burial and resurrection of Christ.

We see in Noah, a just man, perfect in his generations, who walked with God in the same way as Enoch, *that Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord*.

Man has always been saved by grace through faith.

The Bible says in **Hebrews 11**;

*By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.*

But what of man? As the Bible says, man began to multiply on the earth, and daughters were born unto them. The sons of God took the daughters of man, being fair, attractive to the men, and the Lord surmised that man, being flesh would not always strive with Him, and to limit the wickedness of man, God began to shorten man's natural life.

*There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.*

The Bible says there were giants in the earth in those days. And that after that, the sons of God came unto the daughters of man and bare children who were mighty men of renown. Note these are men. Of great stature, no doubt. Same as we see in Goliath, his people, and even occasionally today. The genetic potential of man being what it is, divinely made.

*And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.*

This is God's judgment of man. He is telling us it was the wickedness of man that repented Him of our creation.

God repents, changes His mind given the outcome, and He seeks to destroy them and the earth for it too has become corrupt with the blood of the violence of men. *But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.*

This is the prologue to the generations of Noah.

teachings.title: Abel's blood sacrifice and Cain's works
teachings.summary: Abel was accepted by faith in the blood sacrifice while Cain was rejected for offering his own works, and the shedding of innocent blood cries out from the earth and brings judgment on a land.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 11:4**
*By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.*

Now fallen, cast out from Eden, Adam and Eve, the mother of man are fruitful and multiply.

And her first born, a man from God is Cain, a tiller of the earth. Working the fields.

We know from Genesis 3 the burden God placed on fallen man.

*Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field; In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.*

Cain, under this burden grew herbs and vegetables, fruit of the land. With sweat of his brow. *Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the* Lord*.*

And God respected not his sacrifice.

And Abel, a keeper of sheep, *he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the* Lord *had respect unto Abel and to his offering.*

The firstling lamb. The sacrifice of blood for attornment. The Bible says Abel *by faith* brought the sacrifice that was acceptable unto the Lord.

But Cain brought his works and was rejected.

But God, long suffering and who the Bible says would not that any man perish, gives His word to Cain, to repent towards the faith, in the blood of the lamb for remission of sin, as He had given Adam and Eve, that Abel gained God's pleasure by.

*And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell. And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen? If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.*

Unable to get past his own pride and accept God's promise, His word, Cain allowed his wrath in, and in covetousness slew innocent Abel, and the very earth cries out to the Lord that his blood had been spilled.

This is a Biblical doctrine that's often overlooked. The spilling of innocent blood actually causes the earth itself to cry out to God. We see several times throughout scripture God warns man against it;

*That innocent blood be not shed in thy land, which the LORD thy God giveth thee for an inheritance, and so blood be upon thee.*
**Deuteronomy 19:10**

*For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now*.
**Romans 8:22**

*The blood of their sons and their daughters,*
*Whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan;*
*And the land was polluted with the blood.*
**Psalm 106:38**

One of the things that curses a land and brings judgement on a people is innocent blood shed. It pollutes the land, and the earth travails and groans, crying out to the Lord.

And so undone, Cain is cursed.

When we reject God's word, His gift of salvation in the blood of Christ, the lamb slain at the foundation of the world,  when we count on our works and want credit from God for our own righteousness, we invite sin into our heart, and when we reject God's word finally, are rejected of Him. Marked as Cain.

teachings.title: Then began men to call upon the name of the Lord
teachings.summary: Since the generation of Enos all men have been saved the same way, by faith in the Lord, calling upon His name, as Romans 10:13 and Joel 2:32 declare.
teachings.text:
*And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew. And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the Lord.*

*For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.*
**Romans 10:13**

*And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved.*
**Acts 2:21**

*And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered: for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as the Lord hath said, and in the remnant whom the Lord shall call.*
**Joel 2:32**

The first generation of man had the sure word of God directly to them, of the faith in the Lord to deliver them. The blood sacrifice as atonement. The promise of eternal life in the Lord, who is our salvation.

This is the faith which all man has been saved by, in Christ Jesus, since the world began.

And as Enos' generation came to be, and the faith given the father's by God's word handed down, men began to call upon the name of the Lord for salvation.

Jesus the same yesterday, today and forever.

*But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name.*
**John 1:12**

teachings.title: Sin entered by choice and so does the free gift
teachings.summary: Made in God's image with will, Adam chose to sin and Christ chose to obey, and a free gift cannot be forced but must be received by choice.
teachings.text:
**Romans 5:12-17**
*Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned: (for until the law sin was in the world: but sin is not imputed when there is no law. Nevertheless death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam's transgression, who is the figure of him that was to come. But not as the offence, so also is the free gift. For if through the offence of one many be dead, much more the grace of God, and the gift by grace, which is by one man, Jesus Christ, hath abounded unto many. And not as it was by one that sinned, so is the gift: for the judgment was by one to condemnation, but the free gift is of many offences unto justification. For if by one man's offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.*

And so, sin entered the world by the disobedience of one man, who knowingly violated the one command of God.

Adam, given the perfect situation, abundance of food, dominion, a perfect help meet for a wife, climate so perfect they could be naked, and the purity and innocence to not be ashamed of it. He knew God, could talk with Him and know he was loved by His creator more than anything else in creation. Paradise on earth with none of the cares of this world that we use as excuse and snares to trap us.

And had this been given without choice, without free will, the ability to choose, it would have been a prison. A cosmic dollhouse.

But God, as He made us in His image, made us with the capacity for will. Conscious of our own independent thought. Not simply a biped humanoid with a beard, the shell of the flesh, but like unto Him in that we can think, reason and have an independent soul. And thus, our own will. That is what makes us like unto God, made in his image. God the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit all have will to choose, the Bible tells us, and the Son and the Spirit do the will of the Father, by choice, as Jesus wept in prayer in the garden of Gethsemane, commiting Himself to the Father's will, not Jesus' own.

And so, Adam was given a choice. A law. A commandment to obey, with consequence if he chose not to.

In a garden, man made a choice to sin and disobey the will of God the Father, and in a garden, the Man, Christ Jesus chose to obey unto death.

*For if by one man's offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.*

Sin couldn't enter the world without choice. Sin couldn't be taken from the world without choice. A free gift cannot be received by force, or it is no longer free. It must be accepted by choice.

And so, God's first interaction with man was to provide him a choice. In the first few chapters of the first book of God's word, given to us by Him to know Him. And the choice of fallen man to believe that sure testimony, or not. To be like Eve, who was told of the command by Adam, and instead of believing God's word, was deceived.

teachings.title: Fig leaves of our own works
teachings.summary: Adam and Eve tried to cover their shame with fig leaves of their own making and then blamed others, as men still do instead of trusting God's covering.
teachings.text:
*And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons*.

So, having sinned and felt the conviction in their hearts, they knew they were naked before God, and ashamed. Having the knowledge of good and evil, just as the serpent said, using that seed of truth to say it would make them like God.

This is another favorite deception of the devil, to make us covetous of God, and the false promises that we can become God and usurp His station and take His power for ourselves.

And the first instinct Adam and Eve had, when faced with this feeling of shame, was to attempt to cover it up with their own works. In aprons they made. And like our own works, the fig leaves were insufficient to make them righteous. And seeing that the LORD God was in the garden, they hid from Him, showing that they knew in their hearts their work wasn't enough.

God calls to them, and calls them out for their transgression of the law, (*for sin is the transgression of the law*), and questions them, if they ate of that tree He forbid.

And Adam, like many of us when caught up in sin, blames another, and in fact, blames God.

*The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.*

It's her fault. And you gave me her, so it's really your fault, God!

How often do we rationalize our sins this way? How laughable it is when Adam does it. It's cringe, embarrassing, to see him, who given everything and free will, still has the audacity to blame the God who created him for his own choices.

"Oh if I had this advantage" and "If things were different and I didn't have this pressure on me..." "If this person didn't give me the opportunity, the temptation, oh Lord! The person you brought in to my life, I might add!"

And Eve answers no better; *The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.* Her own covetousness playing no part in her excuse.

How many times in our lives have we, like Adam, blamed the cruel fates and fallen nature of others, and the God who made us for our willful and intentional sin? Or blame the devil for tricking us into doubting God's word, beguiled.

It's as pathetic and stupid as when Adam and Eve do it here.

And how many of us seeking our own righteousness, poorly sow together fig leaves of our own works, seeking to erase the transgressions ourselves. Hiding from God?

teachings.title: He that believeth not shall be damned
teachings.summary: Mark 16:16 does not make baptism required for salvation, since the condition is belief and baptism is only the outward sign of a profession of faith.
teachings.text:
And with Mark's telling of the resurrection, instruction and ascension, we reach the end of his Gospel. It's shortest, often terse, but packs quite a bit of doctrine.

We see the familiar story of Marys going to the tomb on the third day, Sunday morning after the sabbath, (the 3 Sabbaths passed while Jesus was in Hell, doing all the work. Two holy days and one weekly sabbath). They find the tomb apparently unguarded, the stone rolled away and an angel of God, a messenger resembling a young man, sitting in the tomb telling them that Christ is risen. We are told Jesus appears unto Mary Magdalene, and on the road to two others. To the 11. Teaching them in all things.

*Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature. He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be damned.*

This verse is often used to create the false doctrine of baptism being required for salvation, ignoring that the either/or condition is belief. And missing that, missing direct scripture, from Jesus saying that those who believe are saved, those who don't are damned. That's the gospel to be preached to every creature throughout the world.

Not of works or of any other means. Belief in the risen Christ who takes away the sins of the world. Baptism is the outward sign that we may assume someone has professed Christ, calling upon His name and the name of the Father and Holy Spirit. And those that believe not are damned to eternal punishment.

*So then after the Lord had spoken unto them, he was received up into heaven, and sat on the right hand of God*.
Amen

teachings.title: The rich young man and blind Bartimaeus
teachings.summary: The rich young man trusted his own righteousness and riches and left unsaved, while blind Bartimaeus called on the Lord for mercy and was made whole by faith.
teachings.text:
And to the story of the rich young man, presented in **Mark 10** and as we also read in parallel passage of **Matthew 19**, a few weeks ago.

In Mark we see it in slightly different light, as the young man comes off more sincere in this telling, but is identical in result and reason for it.

He begins by flattering Jesus as "good master," and tempting him, Jesus asks why he's called Him good when there is no one good but God.

This truth is important, because it is both a rhetorical question Jesus is using to give the young rich man the opportunity to understand that Jesus is God, for He is good. But also serves to set up the exchange to follow. That there is none righteous by the deeds of the law. There is none that does good. All have fallen short of the glory of God. But as we see, this young man misses both points and asks his original question, "what must I do to gain eternal life?" And he asks this sitting next to the way, the truth and the light, maintaining that he has observed all the commandments of the law since the days of his youth.

He is sitting next to the sinless perfection of Christ, claiming to be 'good.' Jesus, looking upon him with love as it says here in Mark, tells him then, if this is true, "sell all your possessions, give up everything to the poor, and follow me."

And the rich young man declined and goes his own way.

People delude themselves regarding their own righteousness. We consider ourselves more righteous than we are, especially in comparison to other people who we are certain are far worse sinners. And the more possessions we have, the more material wealth, the more we can dilute ourselves into thinking that to have such blessings God must favor us. That we must be doing something right. We develop a pride, a comfort in the material, and neglecting the spiritual, are trapped by our riches.

We have to come to Jesus as little children, who own nothing, are full of trust and wonder, innocent and fearful of God knowing that we're sinners. In contrast, the Rich Young Man comes with a pride and arrogance, and unable to come to the truth about himself or Christ Jesus.

*Children, how hard is it for them that trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of God! It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God. And they were astonished out of measure, saying among themselves, Who then can be saved? And Jesus looking upon them saith, With men it is impossible, but not with God: for with God all things are possible.*

It is impossible for man to be righteous. But with God all things are possible. If you're trusting in anything of this world, you are like a camel trying to pass through the eye of a needle.

Given as contrast to the rich young man, we learn of blind Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, who sat by the highway side begging.

A man with nothing, and further blind of sight.

The rich young man having everything, and being able to look Jesus directly in the eye and not see Him for who He was, compared to a blind beggar, Bartimaeus, who lacking sight, has faith enough to truly see, crying out repeatedly "*Thou son of David, have mercy on me*."

And when Jesus showed mercy on him, asking what he'd have Him do, he replied "Lord, that I might receive my sight." And healing the blind beggar Bartimaeus, Jesus says "Go thy way, thou faith has made thee whole."

But unlike the young man earlier, Bartimaeus, having already obtained eternal life, his faith having made him whole, having called upon the name of the Lord for mercy, leaves what little he has to follow Jesus. (Which is why we know his name)

One man, relying on his own righteousness, unable to see that the Son of David, the Son of man, the Son of God, the Christ, sat beside him. And unable to part with the things of this world, to be healed, to follow Christ, he departs unsaved and damned.

teachings.title: Even the dogs received the crumbs
teachings.summary: Jesus came to take away the sins of the whole world, so salvation is by individual faith and not by flesh and blood, while God judges nations by their collective works.
teachings.text:
I was posting commentary on the Gentile woman who comes to Jesus asking Him to cast The devil out of her daughter, and His telling her that until the children were full, the dogs shouldn't be fed.

Her clever retort that even the dogs catch crumbs as they fall to the floor moves Jesus to mercy and he heals her daughter. This showed both the faith of the woman, and her ability to hear and understand Jesus's parable.

He wasn't literally calling Gentiles dogs in a derogatory way, he was making a point that his earthly ministry was to the Lost tribes of Israel, the sheep that needed to be gathered back to their master.

By showing ears to hear, and understanding she showed that she hears her master's voice.

Many dispensationalists and Jews use these passages and their parallel in other Gospels, to promote a wicked idea that Jesus was for the Jews, and that the conversion of the Gentiles later by the Great Commission was some sort of special boy thing.

Jesus came on his earthly ministry to those who had been given the oracles of god, the words of the prophet, the law written out not just in their hearts but in stone and in parchment, published about. That they should have recognized Him for who He is, the Christ, before He was lifted up on the cross, calling all men unto redemption.

To them much was given. *What advantage then hath the Jew?* This is that advantage.

But in all things, in all ways, Jesus was sent to take away the sins of the whole world.

Now there are many theories as to who represents the true tribes of Israel, and who the Jews who say they are but are not might be. I am not ignorant of them, and I have my own theories and preferences regarding this, that match what many of you believe. But the striving and debate that surround these theories often venture too close to foolish genealogies and Jewish fables. Some of which are a Kaiser Sose effort by Jews to cloud their origin and past, making them out to be more powerful or sinister than they can be. And ideas promoted by others who wish to make salvation one of blood rather than faith, of flesh rather than spirit. This is a huge mistake.

We have individual soul liberty. We are freed in Christ one by one, by a free will faith. And we are also damned by that same free will when we choose not to obey the gospel. And some, not wishing to retain God in their knowledge while here on Earth make the free will choice to harden their hearts and are turned over, given up to reprobation.

Now, some are blessed to be born into a nation of peoples whose hearts are inclined to the Lord.  To us is given the oracles of God. To be born in a Christian majority nation is an advantage similar to that of the Jew in the first century compared to the Greek.

Today we have this advantage over China, India or Israel. And though many of us fail to come to saving faith in Christ, none of our nation is ignorant to his existence and the good news of His resurrection. Amen.

And just as some of us are blessed to be born into a nation inclined towards God, some are born into a nation that so utterly rejects Him, that there are few seeking to find Him.

God judges nations by their collective works, here on earth. He judges man by their faith, individually, for the Kingdom to come.

It is not by flesh and blood that we are saved, but by faith and spirit. Never lose sight of that, regardless of what theory you hold. Even the dogs received the crumbs.

teachings.title: God is just, and God is love
teachings.summary: Scoffers who call God cruel for damning imperfect men are fruit of works religion, but God saves by grace through faith all who believe, as a gift that can never be lost.
teachings.text:
A common refrain of the worldly scoffers that God is "cruel," and "how can a just God sens us to Hell knowing we can't be perfect?"

This ignorance is the bad fruit of the damnable heresies of works-based religions that teach we must earn our way to Heaven, that our own righteousness keeps us from Hell.

There are none righteous no not one. The wages of sin is death. *But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.*

*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.*

God is just. God is love. And He gave us the hope in Christ, that all who believe on Jesus are saved. Just as we are, *sealed unto the day of redemption.* Everlasting life, given as a gift, that can never be lost or taken away. Regardless of our own righteousness, which the Bible says are filthy rags.

*For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the GIFT OF GOD: Not of works, lest any man should boast.*

Even *to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.*

As Jesus, who cannot lie said; *And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand.*

*My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand.*

*I and my Father are one.*

If you have been one of those who felt lost and hopeless because you were told God only saves the righteous, and that if you become Christian, you have to be perfect or face Hell, understand that this is not what the Bible teaches. That there is hope. That God's grace is unto you in Christ just as you are.

teachings.title: Not by works of righteousness which we have done
teachings.summary: Titus 3 makes clear we are saved by grace alone through faith in Christ alone, and good works are for those who have already believed, to be profitable to others.
teachings.text:
Finishing Titus, Paul continues his exhortation to teach sound and profitable doctrine to the Cretians. Letting no man despise Titus for the truth, encouraging him and those who he sets up as pastors and elders in the churches he plants as evangelist to make certain they have the the same doctrines of faith.

This instruction has given us as men, women, girls and boys, servants and slaves, leaders and pastors the blueprint for Christian living. Continuing the theme, Paul writes, again, that we must subject ourselves to higher powers, even as we keep God as the highest. *If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men,* as he writes in Romans.

And again, this is to make us blameless that we may win people who are in error, bringing them to repentance towards God and common salvation. Being a good witness. This is a hard saying, and pride, fear and wrath lead many to stumble at it.

We are warned to speak evil of no man, because after all, the sins and flaws that they may be engaged in are sins common to man, and such were we at times. But with the kindness and mercy God showed us, so too we are to extend grace towards others that they may be drawn to the light. As Jesus taught, *Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.*

And this is the purpose of good works, to be profitable to other men in showing them the light of God. Not to justify us before God, but that others may step into the light by our example. That works are not how we are saved is the clearest, most repeated doctrine in scripture, and yet it continues to be the stumbling block that keeps so many perishing, damned to Hell because they trust in their self righteousness to save them.

It couldn't be any clearer than in Titus 3:

...*That the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward man appeared, Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost; Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour; That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.*

There is no doubt we are saved from our sins and Hell by faith alone, by grace alone, in Christ alone. That God's grace extends to all men. That the renewing of our spirit comes from the Holy Ghost, and He through our faith in Jesus Christ, and God's promise that we be His heirs to the Kingdom of Heaven in the assurance of eternal life.

This is the Gospel. There is nothing more to it. There can be nothing less.

And to put works firmly in the place where they belong, to be encouraged in the life of those who are already saved, that we may be in service to those who have yet to be. (And no, they aren't automatic, as some false prophets preach, for if they were then we wouldn't need so much encouragement to commit ourselves to them)

*This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men.*

This is the Biblical Doctrine of good works. That they which *have believed*, past tense, in the Gospel that was just laid out, *might* do them and be profitable to others.

We are justified by His grace. And so we should be reminded of that and do good works that others may benefit from our salvation.

If your theology is anything else, repent. You're perishing. As wise and as knowledgeable to the doctrines of man as you might be, don't let your pride mislead you from the clear truth presented here, and throughout scripture.

teachings.title: The sheep and the goats: charity shows faith
teachings.summary: The charity of the sheep is how their faith is shown and lived, not the means of entering the Kingdom, and the goats' lack of charity reflects their unregenerate state.
teachings.text:
Rounding out the chapter, Jesus gives us a summation of the end, that He will gather His sheep unto Him, and the goats, the unbelieving, be cast into Hell.

Christ's rationale, that those who are His extended charity to the needy brethren, and by this, perhaps unwittingly as it is painted by Him, did so unto Him;

*Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me...Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.*

Again, works-based heresy puts it that it's these acts of charity, which is the love shown others as a reflection of the light of God, the grace He's shown us magnified by our works is the means of entering into the Kingdom, rather than the way by which our faith is shown. How we are separated from the goats as His sheep. As the Bible says in **James 1**;

*Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.*

Religion is the practice of our faith. This is how it is lived.

And note that the sheep didn't even consider the gain, that it was truly Jesus being helped rather than a stranger. It was just what they did. As Paul reminds us; *Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares*.

And to the goats, Jesus says; *Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye did it not to one of the least of these, ye did it not to me.* The significance of their not having charity in their hearts from God's grace is reflected in their spiritual condition.

teachings.title: The rich young man's self-righteousness
teachings.summary: The rich young man claimed righteousness by the law but would not forsake his riches to follow Christ, showing that pride and self-righteousness keep men from the salvation the poor in spirit receive by faith.
teachings.text:
Next we see another telling of the Rich Young Man who claims righteousness by the law, saying that he has obeyed all the commandments since his youth, but what more must he do to be saved?

He calls Jesus good master, in an act of flattery that Jesus turns around on him handing him a softball on a tee. If only God is good why call me good, Jesus asks. He's taking the compliment and giving a subtle opportunity for the Rich Young Man to say "Because thou art God," which of course will not say, it having been an insincere platitude.

Running through the list of commandments, Jesus asks if he follows them all to which the Rich Young Man assures him that he has his whole life, but when Jesus suggests he sell all that he have giving up everything to follow Him, which would give action to his claim of righteousness, the Rich Young Man balks and departs.

It's this pride and arrogance that Jesus is preaching against throughout the past few chapters. It is more difficult for a rich man to enter the Kingdom of Heaven than it is for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle, because they're carrying that pride with them, their love of the material wealth that they've accumulated, their self-righteousness in thinking that they have adhered to the whole of the law, not just by letter but in spirit, when in truth they're as much a sinner as the beggar, who in faith, inherits the kingdom of God through Christ Jesus.

Had he recognized Jesus as Christ, the son of God, and truly sought the kingdom of Heaven by faith, he would have abandoned his riches and followed Christ, when asked, and in that faith, been saved.

teachings.title: The concrete gospel by which we are saved
teachings.summary: The gospel is a specific thing to believe (God, our sin, death as its wage, Christ's death and resurrection), and adding a required repentance of sin puts a man back under the whole law.
teachings.text:
The gospel of grace and reconciliation by which we believe and are saved, is a concrete understandable and specific thing, spelled out by God hundreds of different ways throughout the Bible.

You must believe there is a God, whose existence is revealed to us in nature, His creation and in the conscience of our hearts.

You must believe that we are sinners. That there are none righteous no not one. This is testified to us in our hearts, our very deeds, our observation of others, and by the schoolmaster that is the law.

We must believe that the punishment for sin is death. We are deserving death and Hell for our transgressions.

We must believe that Jesus is Christ, the Son of God. That He was made flesh, dwelt among us, sinless. That He was persecuted, tortured and killed, descending into hell for 3 days and 3 nights as payment for our transgressions. And that on that third day he rose again, fulfilling the promise God made to man that if they believe, they have eternal life and forgiveness of sins.

Biblical repentance in relation to salvation is always this; turning from whatever else you are relying on, or whatever delusion that you hold that conflicts with the good news of Jesus Christ, and turning towards God and acceptance of this truth to receive that gift of eternal life which can never be lost or taken away.

This faith is never contingent on anything we do, it can't be, for we are not righteous, and God is holy and true.

But to add to this other requirements, to add to this that we must maintain some unmeasurable repentance from sin...Which sins? All sin? Sin of commission? Sins of omission? Thoughts of foolishness? Thoughts of lust? Just major sins like fornication and drunkenness? Adultery?

But what of lies? Being afraid? The Bible says they have a part in the lake of fire along with murderers and whoremongers.

All sin condemns us. Those who say they don't sin are liars according to scripture.

What then? If you believe that you have to work for your salvation, that Jesus needs your help to impute his righteousness over your filthy rags, then what must you do to be saved?

The Bible makes it clear: Keep the whole of the law. But if you offended one point, Hell awaits you.

teachings.title: Cleaning the house without God
teachings.summary: Turning over a new leaf and quitting sins without Christ leaves a man worse off and still judged, for real cleansing only comes through faith in Him.
teachings.text:
One other thing I overlooked, where Jesus teaches about people who clean up their own lives, sitting right themselves without God to cleanse the evil spirits from them, and who, in the end our worse off than had they never made the effort.

There's understanding here, that our simple repenting of sins, so to speak, giving up serious bad habits and addictions and behaviors, alone without God, is vanity. And those who do so may well no longer engage in the behaviors, but yet will suffer judgment just the same.

Real healing comes through Christ and our faith in Him that saves a wretch like us. It's not enough to simply turn your life around. It's not enough to turn over a new leaf. Even the most wicked man among us can quit smoking, or lose 50 lb. Even a reprobate can give generously to a charity. But without God, these efforts are in vain.

teachings.title: I never knew you
teachings.summary: Depart from me, I never knew you proves no saved person loses salvation, and the will of the Father is that whoever sees the Son and believes on Him has everlasting life.
teachings.text:
And thinking themselves righteous, when they come before Jesus touting their works, he says depart from me I never knew you. (Proving you don't lose salvation. He doesn't say he used to know them, but never did)

In verses 21-23, Jesus lays in to those selfish and vain workers of iniquity, but many unsaved people trapped in false doctrine twist this verse to mean you must do works to be saved. "You must do the will of the Father see!"

But what is the will of the Father? Jesus tells us;

*This is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

We are building our house upon the solid rock of the word. Living the sayings of scripture, embodied in Christ. Doing the will of the Father.

Those who ignore scripture, rely on shifting traditions of man and their ever-changing doctrines, are building upon sand.

teachings.title: By grace are ye saved through faith
teachings.summary: Jew and Gentile alike were children of wrath and are saved only by grace through faith, not works, made one new man in Christ with the partition removed.
teachings.text:
Ephesians chapter 1 built the theme of the first 3 chapters; the promise of God, predestinated in Christ and redeemed in us through faith, to be heirs to His Kingdom, and being bestowed with spiritual blessings as His sons.

The immediate application of this for the Galatians and other Gentiles to whom it is written was the Jews attitude towards them, even in the early church. That they were not joint heirs. That they were somehow less than believing Jews in the Kingdom of Heaven, not having been of the "chosen people."

It's one of the reasons for Paul's emphasis on being elect in Christ. Being all chosen to members of the body of which Jesus is the head.

Here in chapter 2, Paul builds on the idea of adoption of grace, to being sons of God, and compares the sonship of believers to the 'children of disobedience,' or the 'children of wrath.' which we all were, Jew or Gentile, without grace from God, His mercy and the blood of Christ, that we who believe are quickened, our spirit born again as His sons.

Even when we were dead in sins, Christ died for us all. That we may sit *together,* raised up *together,* by the grace and mercy of God. Something we all needed to be there, Jew or Gentile. *Together* in Christ. And all bestowed with blessings of the exceeding richness of our Father, given by God's grace.

*For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast.*

Grace is unmerited, unearned and unconditional love. Things given in grace are given not because of anything we have done or who we are, by by faith in Christ, God's gift is made accessible to us all.

Not of circumcision of the flesh, or the law of commandments contained in ordinances. But by grace through faith in God's mercy and Jesus' blood shed for the word.

Paul acknowledges that at times, before Christ, that the Gentiles were "afar off," kept in twain, ignorant of the law and of the promise. But now, *made nigh by the blood of Christ.*

The partition between peoples and who were elect by grace through faith, removed after the coming of Jesus. All saved become a new man. *For through him we both have access by one Spirit unto the Father.*

No more strangers or foreigners, we are all made part of the temple of God, with Jesus as the cornerstone, the foundation laid by the prophets and apostles. Each believer, a pillar.

teachings.title: Stand fast in liberty: Christ shall profit you nothing
teachings.summary: Trusting circumcision or any added work, even partly, makes one a debtor to the whole law so that Christ profits them nothing.
teachings.text:
We who believe are freeborn sons of God, heirs to His Kingdom. Paul exhorts to standfast in that liberty, and not to be drawn back to self-righteousness of sacraments and observances, works and deeds, which is bondage.

If they trust in their circumcision to justify them, even partially, then Christ will profit them nothing. This could be any other work of the flesh you're trusting to save you, even if it is added to faith. Even if it is done in zeal. It makes null the promise. Be it adding baptism, turning from sin, church membership and attendance, rites of man, communion...all things done by those calling themselves Christian by yoking themselves to the bondage of the unregenerate Jew. Christ profits them nothing.

They become debtors to the whole of the law, and there are none righteous, no not one. None who can do the whole of the law. And so they perish. If this is you, you're perishing. Repent.

teachings.title: The works of the flesh indict the law-keeper
teachings.summary: Those keeping circumcision to be saved are still indicted by the works of the flesh, which no ceremony can erase, and only faith gives the inheritance.
teachings.text:
As to the flesh, Paul lists the sins, common to man, that violate the law the Galatians seem eager to put themselves under.

*Adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness, Idolatry, witchcraft, hatred, variance, emulations, wrath, strife, seditions, heresies,*
*Envyings, murders, drunkenness, revellings, and such like: of the which I tell you before, as I have also told you in time past, that they which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God.*

They are counting on their cutting off of foreskin to save them, to adhere to the law to please the Judaizers among them, making them debtors to the whole of the law; meanwhile the lusts of the flesh, made manifest, indict them.

We all have committed adultery, in our hearts if not physically. We envy and covet and engage in emulations, the comparison of ourselves to others in a competitive way. We feel wrath, murder in our hearts, with hatred for others. Plot sedition. Spread heresy.

None of that can be forgiven and erased by keeping a ceremonial part of the law. Carnal ordinances can't get you the inheritance. Only faith can.

And those in faith have crucified our sins so that our flesh may be dead in Christ, but our spirit alive with the risen Jesus.

teachings.title: Not justified by the works of the law
teachings.summary: Galatians 2:16 plainly says no flesh is justified by the works of the law, so anyone depending on turning from sin or keeping ordinances frustrates grace and will perish.
teachings.text:
Far too many frustrate the grace of God by taking it upon themselves to be the author of their own salvation, seeking to justify themselves by their adherence to the law, and this making the sacrifice of Jesus Christ in vain.

**Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.**

This is as clear a verse as there can be, and it is not alone in scripture.

If you are depending on your ability to turn from sin, to follow the law of God or the carnal ordinances to be saved...any of the things of the old covenant that served as a school master in teaching man cannot obtain righteousness except through grace, given as a gift, imputed by God from Christ...you will perish.

Salvation comes only in faith that God's grace has given us His only begotten Son, through whom is remission of sins. Period.

teachings.title: Washed and sanctified, not saved by quitting sin
teachings.summary: 1 Corinthians 6 is no proof of repent-of-your-sins salvation, because Paul says we are washed and justified in Christ, and our liberty means sin is not expedient and harms us, not that we lose the kingdom.
teachings.text: Others, stripping the context of taking matters before secular judgment, draw out a doctrine of Repent of your sins-works salvation. That "see if you engage in these sins, you're not saved. You won't inherit the kingdom of God!" This ignores the following verses in which Paul says that we are washed and sanctified in Christ, not by how well we can quit sinning. That, as Paul says, "all things are lawful" to us, but not expedient. We have liberty from our sin through Jesus, but it's not in our best interests to willfully sin, especially fornication. That there's a cost. That it's harmful, because God has made it so. There are consequences for abusing yourself this way should we take this liberty to fornicate like a harlot, God forbid.

teachings.title: The Bible way to heaven: faith alone
teachings.summary: Through John and Acts the one message is that sinners are saved by believing on Christ crucified and risen, not by works or a denomination, and that this free gift sealed by the Spirit can never be lost.
teachings.text:
Before beginning another book of the Bible, I just want to reflect back on what we have seen consistently: In John, the only book written explicitly to the unsaved that they may believe and receive eternal life, where in every chapter, Jesus teaches that it is by faith alone we are saved. In Acts, the Apostles from Pentecost, unto Paul, decades later in Rome, this message has been the same.

We are all sinners, deserving death and Hell, but God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son that whosever believeth on Him shall not perish but have everlasting life. That Jesus was Christ, crucified and risen. That by calling upon His name, we are adopted as sons of God, heirs to the promise of the kingdom, and this free gift, given in God's grace can never be lost or taken away.

It is this faith that saves us. Not our works. Not a denomination. Not anything other than believing in your heart this truth of the good news. That once we do, our spirit, dead in sin is quickened by the Holy Spirit, and we are sealed by Him unto the day of judgment, our sins washed clean in Jesus' blood, we are healed by his stripes.

This is the good news. This is the Gospel.

If you are not 100% sure today that if you were to die, you would go to heaven, please listen to this presentation of the Bible way to heaven. For faith comes by hearing and hearing by the word of God.

teachings.title: What must I do to be saved
teachings.summary: To the Philippian jailer's question Paul answers only believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, with no repenting of sins, surrender, church or sacrament: faith alone, plus nothing.
teachings.text:
But continuing in Acts 16 for now, we see their travels to Phrygia and Galatia, and that they were *forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia,* and later when they were thinking about going into Bithynia, *the Spirit suffered them not.* The Holy Spirit was directing them to where they needed to be, just as He does with us, today when we listen.

They travel to Philippi in Macedonia, meeting Lydia and winning her and her house to Christ.

While abiding there, they are plagued by a girl being used as a soothsayer by corrupt men, pimping out her services, and it is revealed to Paul she is possessed when, mocking, she follows behind them in public "*These men are the servants of the most high God, which shew unto us the way of salvation.*" After days of this Paul casts out the devil in her in Jesus name and this angers the men who'd used her plight to their gain, so much so they bring Paul and Silas to the magistrates and falsely accused them, with the mob behind them, demanding punishment. The magistrates order Paul and Silas scourged and imprisoned.

And yet we see them, bloody with stripes and shackled at the feet imprisoned in the darkest hole of a Philippian jail singing songs and praises of God at midnight.

And while they rejoiced in their suffering there was a mighty earthquake which rent the walls of the prison down. The Philippian jailer who had to have been marveling at their faith prior to this comes out in a panic, ready to kill himself for fear that the prisoners had escaped. But Paul and silas, despite being freed remained behind and Paul calls out stopping the Philippian jailer from falling on his sword

And here we get yet another wonderful example of bringing someone to Christ with the gospel of faith.

The Philippian jailer asks *what must I do to be saved?*

This is the fundamental question. This is the doctrine of the Gospel being asked for, and Paul answers, not with long-winded theological points or esoteric hints at salvation being some sort of Gnostic journey. He doesn't tell him he must repent of his sins, or surrender his life to the Lord Jesus and have his fruit inspected by others. He doesn't tell him he must join a certain Church, or attend mass, or receive sacraments.

"Sirs, what must I do to be saved?"

*And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved.* Simple as.

And accepting this gift of salvation, the Philippian jailer brings Paul and Silas to his home, where they give the gospel to his family and bringing them all to Christ, baptizing them in his name.

Amen.

We are saved by faith alone, plus nothing minus nothing. Not by our works, not by tradition and ceremony, as we saw in the last chapter. We are saved by the blood of Christ who did it all for us, which is given as a gift of Grace by God.

teachings.title: The Jerusalem council and the Judaizers
teachings.summary: Acts 15 rejects the Judaizers' circumcision and law-keeping for salvation, while the letter's precepts on idols, fornication and blood were for sanctification, not salvation.
teachings.text:
In Acts 15 we see the early Christians in the independent churches of Asia Minor were being led astray by Judaizing heretics, trying to bring those saved by grace through faith back under the yoke of law, and through the rite of circumcision. That they were trying to mix grace with works, with "repenting of sin" through obedience to the law, including the carnal ordinances and dietary laws of Moses, and by physical circumcision, which could be considered like unto baby baptism, or any other of the so-called sacraments false churches add to the Gospel as a requirement.

We see Paul and Barnabas return to Jerusalem an an assembly of Apostles and the appointed elders, deacons of the church there at Jerusalem. Some believing Pharisees, retaining a bit of their holier than thou ways, have joined in demanding Gentiles circumcise.

 Peter speaking against the judaizers, reminds them that they as Jews could not attain perfection through the law, only by believing in the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ shall any be saved.

God through His word continues to hammer home that the only salvation is through faith, delivered through God's grace, in the name of Jesus. Not of works of the law. Not of what we do.

James, who takes charge of the assembly (not 'Pope Peter'), gives scripture to answer to the issue. This is what we should all do when faced with a question regarding anything. Search the scriptures and see what God has to say.

James recommends and the others agree, to instead write edifying epistles to the churches, to tell them that these judaizers are wrong, that the law is past, but to remind and encourage them that they should continue to avoid idols, the meat sacrificed to them by their country men, fornication, and consumption of blood, (all of which we see in later epistles, being instructed to the churches), that *they may do well.* These are given as percepts for behavior and sanctification, not as requirements for salvation, given to avoid confusion, especially with those Gentiles who had been in synagogue prior to believing on Christ, and were familiar with the law of Moses. They attempt to head off future contentions by indicating that these things still should be avoided.

Now idolatry and fornication had been of old, God's law. Before Moses. And the restrictions on blood and strangulation, from Noah. These were not done away with in Christ the way the temple sacrifice, diverse washings, circumcision and the levitical priesthood were, and we will see this explained in the Epistles of Paul in greater detail.

The Apostles send these letters and emissaries, Judas and Silas with Paul and Barnabas to visit these churches and add weight to the doctrine being preached.

The chapter ends after some time has past, and the pair of evangelists reflect on making a trip to visit the various churches they'd helped plant among the Gentiles, and we see the falling out they had regarding Mark, who had previously been taken with them on their missionary journey, and we are told he had bailed at Pamphylia when it got tough. Paul doesn't want him along, Barnabas does and the long time friends in Christ part ways.

We see that even those of one accord in the faith don't always see eye to eye, and differences of opinion and strife strike even the best men of God.

teachings.title: Peter and Paul preached one gospel
teachings.summary: Peter's words at Jerusalem show his gospel is the same as Paul's and Christ's: saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus by faith, not the law.
teachings.text:
*Peter rose up, and said unto them, Men and brethren, ye know how that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe. And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us; And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.*
*Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear? But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they.*

This is the Gospel of faith. Peter's doctrine does not differ from Paul's and neither is different from what Jesus preached.

Far too many prideful and foolish unsaved men falsely claim that "Paul taught different doctrines" and that Peter, as 'pope' taught 'repenting of sin' because he told Jews who crucified Jesus in unbelief to repent and believe. They will misquote cherry picked verses, and ignore those that undermines or completely contradicts their nonsense. But when we read the whole word of God, chapter after chapter, in context and see that it couldn't be clearer that we are justified by faith in the work of Christ, and in His blood we receive the remission of sins.

teachings.title: Whosoever believeth shall receive remission
teachings.summary: Peter's gospel to Cornelius offers remission of sins to whosoever believes, with no turning from sin, works or sacrament.
teachings.text:
Now, introductions and explanations are given as to how this meeting came about, through messengers of God. Peter begins to preach the life of Jesus Christ and the gospel, the good news of his being sent by God. That he lived, preached, was killed by the Jews (every chapter so far has a reference to Jews violence and murder), and that Jesus rose from the dead, bodily, eating and drinking to those who give witness. That Jesus commanded the disciples to preach Christ to the people, that Jesus was who all the prophets who had come before gave witness to. And that though Jesus' name, *whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins.*

This is a clear presentation of the Gospel of faith by which we are saved, given by Peter considered the greatest of possible by many. There is no mention of turning from sin, nor of works, nor of sacrament or ceremony. But whosoever, meaning anyone, believeth in him, that faith alone, shall receive remission of sins. Amen.
