But to be justified before man, that outward sign of his faith, made his faith more perfect. There was a visible tangible act of faith, works that a man may say that they've been shown his faith.

teachings.title: Delivered and translated into the kingdom
teachings.summary: Colossians 1 shows God has already delivered, redeemed and reconciled believers the moment they believed, so we should be thankful and extend that grace to others.
teachings.text:
**Colossians 1:9-15**
*For this cause we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding; That ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God; Strengthened with all might, according to his glorious power, unto all patience and longsuffering with joyfulness; Giving thanks unto the Father, which hath made us meet to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light: Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son: In whom we have redemption through his blood, even the forgiveness of sins*

Be thankful that God has already done so much for us that have been justified in Christ, while we were yet sinners.

God has already made us *partakers of the inheritance of the saints*, *delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son*, and so, *we have redemption through his blood, even the forgiveness of sins*.

As in verse 20-21; *having made peace through the blood of his cross, by him to reconcile all things unto himself; by him, I say, whether they be things in earth, or things in heaven. And you, that were sometime alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works, yet now hath he reconciled*

We are now reconciled, having made peace with the Father through the blood of the Son.

This is the good news, the glory of the Gospel of God. All of these promises have been fulfilled already, the moment you believed and received the baptism of the Spirit, quickening your spirit and sealing you into redemption.

*As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk ye in him.*

Amen. Let us give glory to the Lord Jesus for this, and to God the Father for having the grace and mercy towards us that all these things have been predestined for those who place their trust in Christ.

Knowing this peace and forgiveness and reconciliation, knowing this grace and mercy, let us extend it to our brothers, and to others that they know of our conversion, and hear the gospel on which we stand by faith.

Amen

teachings.title: Therefore being justified by faith
teachings.summary: Justified by faith we have peace with God now and stand in grace, and even glory in tribulations that work patience, experience and hope.
teachings.text:
Therefore.

When we see this word we have to ask ourselves "what's it there for?" What does it refer back to?

Well, 4 chapters of Paul logically and with irrefutable proof from scripture that all are under sin and need salvation, and that salvation is through faith in Jesus Christ, by the grace of God.

Therefore. Therefore what?

*Being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.*

As the heavenly hosts proclaimed in the hills of Bethlehem at the birth of the man Christ Jesus;

*Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.*

The peace and goodwill on earth was come from God to man. Not the peace of men not warring. Not goodwill between tribes. But the enmity of wrath in the transgressions of man made justified by the peace offering of His only begotten Son.

We are justified by faith alone. There is nothing more noted. We have already concluded that by the works of the law no man shall be justified. We already know that by faith, Abraham became father to all who believe. We already know that the judgment of God is upon Jew and Greek alike. And that Jesus as propitiation for our sin has given us salvation from the wrath we deserve.

*Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.*

What's more; By faith we have access into the grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God.

Believing, we are given grace, and by grace, God is given the glory for our salvation. Note, "wherein we stand." This isn't the future, this isn't a process. This is now, at the time of our repentance towards belief in Christ as our redeemer we then, at that moment, stand in grace. And rejoice.

And we not only rejoice in the glory of God's grace that provides us with salvation through faith, because it shows the mercy and judgment and righteousness of God (which remember is one way His glory is revealed to man from Heaven), we also glory in tribulations here on earth, knowing they are a refining fire; that worketh patience, which brings experience, and experience brings hope. Hope builds faith.

*Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen*.

Hope is the sure knowledge that a thing will be that is not yet. The object of faith. Tribulation in our lives, not only persecution for our faith, but just general troubles like health, finance, whatever things common to all men, saved or unsaved, all of it gives opportunity to glorify the Lord, as it makes our faith sharper as we are brought out of it by His mercy and blessings, better for having experienced it.

And our hope is fufifiled in the love of God, by the comforter, the Holy Ghost, which is given us, who indwells with us, quickening our spirit and leading us to that peace which passes all understanding, even in turmoil and crisis.

Our faith in man, traditions, our own works, all will leave us ashamed at some point. But the hope we have in Christ Jesus will never bring us shame. God never lets us down.

teachings.title: While we were yet sinners
teachings.summary: God showed His love by Christ dying for His enemies, so much more shall the reconciled be saved by His life and spared wrath.
teachings.text:
And how do we know that God's word is good, that our hope is true? Because

*But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us*.

That when we were still enemies, working inequities, dead in sin, God reconciled us through the death of His Son. God loved His enemies, and offered the free gift of salvation by the shedding of blood of His only begotten Son.

Think about this, for in it is the righteousness of God.

And if He offered us such a gift, if a righteous man gave His life for us while we were enemies, dying for us while we were dead in sin, then how much more shall He do for us whom have been reconciled to Him in faith by the death of His Son? Who stand in His grace? We shall be saved by His life in the resurrection.

And not only so, that we shall know we will be saved out of tribulation by His resurrection and the promise of God to us likewise for eternal life, but we also joy, rejoice, in God through our Lord Jesus Christ by whom we have now received the atonement.

Our hope is that, today we who believe are spared wrath for our sins, adopted to the promise, and that in tribulation on this earth we will be saved by God's love for His sons, because of the atonement of Christ Jesus that we holdfast to in faith. Amen

teachings.title: Jesus' torment in Hell for our sins
teachings.summary: Jesus spent the days after the cross in Hell bearing the sins of the world as the propitiation, which few Christians care to reflect on.
teachings.text:
We should consider that at this point that first holy week, that Jesus was spending His first full day in Hell, carrying the sins of the whole world. Each moment of torment must have felt like a lifetime; Jesus, as the burnt offering, the Holocaust, the propitiation of our sins that we may be justified in Him. He had 2 more full days to follow.

Many Christians gladly celebrate Easter, rejoicing that He is risen. Some will consider the pain and suffering of the cross. Few want to reflect on His torment in Hell for our sins. He who knew no sin, paying the price for us.

It's something we should reflect on.

teachings.title: One Offering Perfected For Ever
teachings.summary: Christ's one offering cleanses the conscience forever, and the conscience marks three states of man: guilty, cleansed, or seared in reprobation.
teachings.text:
Now having established that Jesus Christ, the Son of God seated at the right hand of the Father, is greater than the angels, greater than Moses, Abraham, David, in all ways, better than the Levites and the descendants of Aaron as the High Priest after the order of Melchisedek, Paul continues to show the superiority of Christ to the Mosaic law itself, which is a picture of His glory. That faith in Him that saves and the promises made of God for that faith, a better covenant. A new and better testament.

Better than the commandments which condemn us, transgressions of the law being sin, better than the dead works which cannot save us and Jesus as our redeemer is a better sacrifice than all the sacrifices offered under the law.

The entire epistle is an appeal to the superiority and primacy of Christ Jesus as our Lord, High Priest, advocate, and sole means of the cleansing of our sins, in either dispensation. Man has always been saved by grace through faith in Christ. The blood of bulls and goats never took away sins. It was not possible, the Bible says. No sacrifice other than Christ cleans the conscience. And so those who yearly sought forgiveness by sin offering rather than as a picture of their faith, fruitlessly returned year after year seeking to clean their conscience.

A conscience, or "with knowledge," offended by sin, knowingly transgressing the law, with understanding, can only be made clean with the blood of Christ. The vail only removed by His flesh, offered for us. A better sacrifice, done once and forever. Taking on the sins of the whole world.

Burnt offerings and sacrifice for sin gave God no pleasure, but Jesus doing the will of the Father, to become sin and die for us that all may be called and those that believe be saved, sanctified once and for all in the offering of Jesus Christ's body. In this the LORD delights.

For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified.

Practical application of this, the implications of this, that we are forgiven of all sin by this perfect sanctification, total remission, forever, is that we be freed from the burden of guilt and the fear of judgment that we may serve the living God.

Faith in Christ is to be born again, our spirit without sin. The Holy Ghost as witness that we can let go of the sins of the past and have full assurance of forgiveness for sins of the flesh going forward. The knowledge that God so loved us, He offered His only begotten Son. The rest that is found in Christ. The true Sabbath.

*This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them; And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.*

*Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin....*

Most of our troubles as man come from the carrying of that burden. The heavy yoke of the conscience. The fear of judgment and death. The pangs of guilt are the Spirit, bringing us reproof of sin that we may understand the need for salvation, and pricked by the hearing of His word, come to understanding and in that knowledge, repent unto faith.

But for some, who taste that heavenly knowledge, partake in the rebuke of the Holy Ghost, reject it. Resenting being judged. Clinging to the trauma, reveling in their sin. And they willfully sin knowing the judgment of God, rejecting Christ and being made reprobate by God. Having their conscience seared as with hot iron.

These are the three spiritual states of man. Unsaved, saved and reprobate. And the underlying condition of fallen man comes in our conscience; be it guilty, cleansed by the blood, or seared by God for our hardened heart.

teachings.title: Christ Offered Once to Bear Our Sins
teachings.summary: Substitutionary atonement teaches that Christ's blood, pictured by the old sacrifices, sealed the better testament and removed the veil between God and man.
teachings.text:
Substitutionary atonement, also called vicarious atonement, the Biblical understanding Jesus Christ being the sacrifice that takes away the sins of the whole world, to the salvation of those who believe, is laid out here (and throughout scripture) as the blood needed to affirm the promise made by God the Father. Just as the blood of bulls and goats was used to seal the covenant with Moses, or marked by Abraham with his promise from God.

But these sacrifices were for a time and a place and acted as a picture for the perfect sacrifice of Jesus Christ, Whose blood marked the promise of a better testament, one in which the separation from God pictured by the temple, the veils, the Levitical priests, dietary laws, marking of days and carnal ordinances of the Old Testament is done away with.

Here at the end of the world, Jesus was offered once and put away sin by the sacrifice of Himself. And in doing so, became our High Priest, and we who believe adopted sons, a holy priesthood. The separation from God is gone. The veil torn asunder.

Many false religions posing as Christians deny the idea that Jesus was the sacrifice that gave us the offer of God's mercy. They deny the grace of a loving God who bought them with the price of His Son. That the shedding of blood and the remission of sins isn't the way, but instead these thorns and briars produce evil fruit that cannot repent from dead works to serve the living God.

But the Bible teaches us the truth of the matter. That Jesus as the sole mediator between God and man was by the means of His death, becoming sin for the redemption of transgressions. (For sin is the transgression of the law).

A testament having no power while the testator liveth. And so the death of the testator signified that those called had come into their promised inheritance. Amen.

So Christ was offered once to bear our sins. And those of us who believed look to His coming to our day of redemption. The Spirit as the surety of the promise, a testimony within us to the truth of God's word.

teachings.title: Princes under tutors until the adoption
teachings.summary: Proverbs for kings and princes are for saved believers, co-heirs who will rule with Christ, since the adoption, the placing as sons, comes at the resurrection, the redemption of the body.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 25** introduces a section (chapters 25–29) of Solomon’s proverbs that were compiled by King Hezekiah's officials, approximately 250–270 years after Solomon's reign.

Hezekiah, the son of the wicked king, Ahaz, began a revival and reformation, tearing down altars and idols. In the first month of his reign, Hezekiah opened and repaired the doors of the House of the Lord. He commanded the Levites to "sanctify" themselves and carry *forth the filthiness out of the holy place*. He restored the observance of Passover. He brought order to the Levites, and proclaimed tithes and offerings from the people.

And in his zeal, the young king commanded scribes to write these sayings of Solomon, that they be preserved and observed.

They begin with the honor of kings to search out the hidden things of God.

**1 Corinthians 2:10**
*But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.*

As I have previously stated, my opinion is that the wisdom for princes and kings is for the saved, as co-heirs with Christ. Even the least in the Kingdom of Heaven is a prince, who will judge with Him in the millennium. We will judge angels. The study of the word is like unto princes under tutors, until the day of adoption. The resurrection where we come into our power as glorified sons of God.

**Galatians 4**
*Now I say, That the heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all; But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father*.

The context here is the law bringing man to understand the need for a savior, but the application mirrors the process of a prince coming into his own by instruction, until the determined time of the King.

As Paul writes in **Romans 8:23** ...*even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.* The day of redemption, the resurrection, is the day of our adoption; the time of the giving of the inheritance, to rule and reign with Jesus.

The Greek word Paul uses for 'adoption,' *huiothesia*, carries a heavier legal meaning than our modern idea of adoption. In that context, it wasn't about bringing an outsider into a family; it was the formal ceremony, the "placing as a son," where an heir reached the age of maturity, the father publicly recognized them as a legal adult, granting them the full authority, a signet ring, and power to manage the estate, or the lands appointed them.

We become sons of God when we are born again, but notice the adoption is at the resurrection. At the day of redemption.

So, when we see proverbs about kings or princes, about judgement and mercy, who to be influenced by, who to seek counsel from...it is all instructions from THE King, God our Father, to His children, who will inherit the Kingdom.

teachings.title: Who are the sons of God?
teachings.summary: Scripture defines the sons of God as believers who receive Christ and are adopted as joint heirs with Him, from Seth's day to now.
teachings.text:
And so, who are the sons of God? The Bible says *as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name.*

Believers. Those that call upon the name of the Lord.

*For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God. And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together. For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us. For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God. For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected the same in hope, Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.*

Those born again into the promise, adopted sons, heirs to the Kingdom of the Lord.

Adopted now, as in the days of Seth and Enos and Enoch and even Noah; *That ye may be blameless and harmless, the sons of God, without rebuke, in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, among whom ye shine as lights in the world.*

*Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God!*

Take comfort in this knowledge, joy in the incomprehensible love God has shown us, that we may be adopted joint heirs with His only begotten Son, Christ Jesus.

*Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is.*

We know that all who believe are the sons of God. That we appear before God in Heaven to present ourselves before the Lord. When God laid Jesus as the cornerstone of our salvation, the angels sang and all the sons of God shouted for joy. And in Christ Jesus God has made His covenant with man, that He *will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.*

teachings.title: Then are the children free
teachings.summary: As kings take tribute from strangers not their children, believers are free sons who pay nothing to enter the kingdom, yet as sojourners still pay tribute to whom it is due.
teachings.text:
The second story told in the chapter is one of tax collectors seeking tribute from Peter for him and Jesus. Peter rightly tells them that he will make good on the payment of tribute to whom tribute is due. And he goes and asks Jesus on the matter. Jesus takes the time to teach an important lesson regarding salvation and the inheritance obtained by our faith.

He asks Peter *of whom do the kings of the earth take custom or tribute? of their own children, or of strangers?* Peter replies, "Strangers."

*Jesus saith unto him, Then are the children free.*

We who are saved by grace through faith are adopted as sons of God, heirs to His promise and the Kingdom of Heaven. We are free of custom and duty, tribute and tax.

Our entrance to the kingdom is free, for we are at Liberty in Christ. We pay nothing, not our works or labors or deeds. It is a gift of God given to all who believe.

But while we sojourn here on earth, we pay tribute to whom tribute is due, and render custom to whom custom is due, because we are sojourning here, strangers in the land. Princes of a better country. Amen

teachings.title: All believers are saints
teachings.summary: Saint is the New Testament title for every believer, not a rank Rome bestows for works, and the peace announced at Christ's birth is peace between God and men through grace.
teachings.text:
Another point to make regarding the introduction, that Paul addresses to the saints and believers, terms which are interchangeable in the New Testament. All believers are saints. It's a title bestowed throughout to all who believe. It is not a select few whose Works were so good that they are honored here on Earth with the title. By making a church of man the arbiter, and basing it on works, the Catholic church has cheapened the term. I am a saint. If you believe you are a saint as well. Even if your backslidden, even if you need to turn from sins that are consuming your life. And as saints we should turn from sin, we should live a righteous life as possible. Live up to it.

Secondly Paul frequently writes that he prays for Grace from God to us the reader, and with that grace, peace.

The only piece we have with God is through his grace, and Christ Jesus. At the nativity the Angels announced peace on Earth. Goodwill towards men. This is a message from God to man, that he is granting them peace with Him, and goodwill through the birth of Jesus. The angel isn't saying that they'll be peace upon the Earth between men, but rather peace between God and men.

teachings.title: Sons of the freewoman, not the bondwoman
teachings.summary: Believers are adopted heirs freed from the tutors of the law, and as Isaac and Ishmael show, those born of the Spirit inherit while those under the bondage of works are cast out.
teachings.text:
Building upon the doctrine that we who believe God are adopted by God, sons according to the promise; being heirs. Continuing that thought, Paul makes the comparison of the law vs grace, that the son can be heir but under a schoolmaster, tutors and governors, yet in the fullness of time, be as the Lord, an inheritor of all. So to, he's saying, the Israelites were when under the law, children of the promise, not come into their inheritance. Now, with the fullness of Christ, all who believe are adopted and freed from the burden of the law, of the tutors and governess, to their inheritance.

Paul explaining this in these terms, as laid out in Hebrew scripture that they may understand, given there are Jews pushing the Galatians to go back under that bondage. Paul says he's afraid of the Galatians that they may be so easily led to a false gospel, that he questions if they even were saved. That we who believe have the Spirit of the Son within us. That we have that quickened spirit, born again crying "Abba!"(Father) to God. They should know better. They should recognize the error. Yet they don't, and so Paul has to assume his labor in preaching the Gospel of grace was in vain, that they aren't saved.

He reminds them that before his preaching the word to them, they served idols, living as heathens, and these judaizers come in and return them to superstition, marking sabbaths and holy days done away with in Christ. Returning them to the bondage of works based salvation.

He reminds them of when he was present with them, the zeal for the Gospel they held, that in spite of a physical infirmity, apparently with Paul's eyes, they readily accepted him to the point they'd have plucked out their own eyes to right his. But now he's their enemy for telling them the truth. He compares winning them to Christ with travails of a mother in birth, and says he's willing to do it to bring them to salvation.

Changing gears, and having established that our salvation is one of adoption, blessing and inheritance from the Father, he asks those who are going back to the OT if they even know it, and uses an example from the Law, the story of Isaac and Ihsmael. How, as told in Genesis 17, Abraham had a son, Ishmael, with a slave woman, Hagar, by natural means, and Isaac with his wife Sara, by spiritual means. When Issac was still an infant, Ishmael teased him, and Sara demanded Abraham to kick Hagar and the boy out, denying him any share of inheritance.

Thus we who are born again in the Spirit become heirs, while those trying to work their way into the kingdom, those under bondage, are denied.

*Now we, brethren, as Isaac was, are the children of promise.*

And, again as Ishmael the son of the flesh persecuted Isaac, son of the Spirit, so to now the Jews after the flesh are misleading them, persecuting the heirs in Christ.

*Nevertheless what saith the scripture? Cast out the bondwoman and her son: for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the freewoman. So then, brethren, we are not children of the bondwoman, but of the free.*

teachings.title: The vanity of riches before death
teachings.summary: Wise and fool, rich and poor all die, riches cannot ransom a soul, and only the fear of the Lord and redemption through Christ give hope in the day of wrath.
teachings.text:
Psalm 49 is a meditation on the futility of life, in the building of of riches, honor and name, when death awaits everyone, rich or poor, wise or fool.

This reflection on life's vanities ties to Solomon's writings in **Ecclesiastes**, from the call to harken to the preacher to the vanity of life and the only remedy, fearing the Lord and receiving His blessing.

**Ecclesiastes 2:16**
*For there is no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; seeing that which now is in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And how dieth the wise man? as the fool.*

This echoes the same sentiment found in verse 10;

*For he seeth that wise men die, likewise the fool and the brutish person perish, and leave their wealth to others.*

**Ecclesiastes 5:15**
*As he came forth of his mother's womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.*

Solomon learned at the feet of his father, and after careful study of all the things his wealth and power availed him of, with the wisdom above other men, granted by God's grace, he would come to the same conclusions David sang of.

The call to incline your ear to hear wisdom, to listen to the dark sayings and parables. To seek understanding is a major theme of Solomon's **Proverbs**;

**Proverbs 4:7**
*Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.*

David teaches us the same lessons in Psalms. The wisdom of God is most valuable, because in that knowledge we may find eternal life.

David expresses confidence in his salvation. He is not afraid when the time comes to be given the wages of his sin, the iniquity of his heels, the death that awaits us all, the consequences of our own making.

Why should we fear in the days of evil, that comes our own making? He knows his redemption is a gift of God. But the man trusting his riches has no hope at all in that day. They cannot redeem themselves or their brothers, and cannot pay the ransom due God for their sins.

Again, this idea that man's riches are worthless in the judgment, that they do nothing for the dead, is repeated by Solomon;

**Proverbs 11:4**
*Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.*

**Proverbs 27:24**
*For riches are not for ever: and doth the crown endure to every generation?*

Their way is folly. The wise man dies like the fool, like the brute, and all their wealth is left for others. But the precious redemption of the soul, that one lives forever and shall not see corruption, that is of God, through faith in the Lord Christ Jesus.

**1 Timothy 2:5–6**
*For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus; Who gave himself a ransom for all, to be testified in due time.*

David laments the fact that worldly prosperity deceives the wealthy, their own riches fooling them into a false sense of security. This is the larger context of the preaching of Christ;

**Matthew 19:23–26**
*Then said Jesus unto his disciples, Verily I say unto you, That a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven. And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God. When his disciples heard it, they were exceedingly amazed, saying, Who then can be saved? But Jesus beheld them, and said unto them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.*

The only hope of man, rich or poor, is God. Only in Him is salvation possible.

**Proverbs 15:16**
*Better is little with the fear of the Lord than great treasure and trouble therewith.*

The blessings of this life are not a hope for the next. The praise of men is vanity before the Throne of an almighty and holy God.

Agur's  prayer in **Proverbs** directly addresses this wisdom;

**Proverbs 30:8-9**
*Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.*

teachings.title: Praise, thanksgiving, confession, deliverance
teachings.summary: We cannot acknowledge salvation without acknowledging the sin we are saved from, and David's psalm models praise, confession, deliverance and judgment in prayer.
teachings.text:
Having acknowledged all He has done for us, and encouraging ourselves and others to turn to Him for salvation through the blessing of the Lord, David's Psalm turns introspective. He confesses the sin that has beset him, and compasses him about with the repercussions of it.

*Withhold not thou thy tender mercies from me, O LORD: let thy lovingkindness and thy truth continually preserve me. For innumerable evils have compassed me about: mine iniquities have taken hold upon me, so that I am not able to look up; they are more than the hairs of mine head: therefore my heart faileth me.*

We cannot acknowledge salvation without acknowledging what God is saving us from.

Just as David and Paul write of having the law written in their heart, and delighting in His word, they both lament the sinful flesh that requires a Savior.

**Romans 7:24–25**
*O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death? I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin.*

We ask they the Lord deliver us. That it is His will that be done. That those who are moved to scorn, mocking our trust in the Lord be made ashamed.

That God use us to shame those that wish to do us evil, to His glory.

Praise, thanksgiving, confession, deliverance, and destruction of those who hold the truth in unrighteousness. This is a model of prayer. That His will be done on earth as it is in Heaven.

And in the end, the joy of His salvation overwhelming us with gratitude and praise, that such a holy and Almighty God takes heed of our prayers and notices us. Loving us so much, while we are yet sinners. Thinking of us. Providing for us. Delivering us.

*Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: let such as love thy salvation say continually, The LORD be magnified. But I am poor and needy; yet the Lord thinketh upon me: thou art my help and my deliverer; make no tarrying, O my God.* Amen

teachings.title: Delight in the saints, not Lordship salvation
teachings.summary: Calling Jesus Lord is a saved believer's statement of fact, not the false gospel of Lordship salvation; our good works add nothing to God but are poured out in love and service to the saints.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 16** presents another sacred hymn celebrating the Lord's salvation, the eternal security of the believer, and the promise of the risen Christ.

The preservation of the saints is the hope of all who place their trust in God. Our very being cries out to Him for salvation, recognizing He is Lord.

Note here that this isn't "Lordship salvation," a false gospel that says you must "make Jesus the Lord of your life" to be saved. It is saved believers, already trusting Him to save us, recognizing that He IS the Lord, as a statement of fact.

David writes, *Thou art my Lord: my goodness extendeth not to thee; But to the saints that are in the earth, and to the excellent, in whom is all my delight.* The good that we do isn't for Him, it adds nothing to the holy and perfect God.

The idea that Jesus needs us to make Him Lord, that by our "turning from sin," we justify ourselves before God, is hubris. It's a false gospel.

The good we do comes from Him, and is poured out to the brothers and sisters, the saints. We benefit others, and they glorify God. We obey His judgements, to one another's profit.

**Matthew 5:16**
*Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.*

We submit ourselves to the righteousness of God. We do not seek to establish our own righteousness, but to magnify His.

**Romans 10:3–4**
*For they being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.*

David's burden is for the saints in the earth, his delight is to the excellent of God. Just as we are commanded to.

**John 13:34–35**
*A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another. By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.*

While we should seek to live peaceably with all men, we should especially look with love upon our fellow believers.

**Galatians 6:9–10**
*And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not. As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith.*

This is the message that we have heard from the beginning. It is our job as Christians. It is how we are to know one another. Not keeping to ourselves or seeking out own profit. Certainly not by hating our brothers.

1 John 3:10–11
*In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother. For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another.*

This is the mind of Christ, to be servants, one to another. To delight in others.

The ultimate expression of humility isn't thinking less of yourself, but not thinking of yourself at all. And the humbleness of submission to God's righteousness should naturally turn to our service for others. Not to add to God's goodness our filthy rags, but to glorify His goodness in us.

teachings.title: Set me as a seal upon thine heart
teachings.summary: The seal on the heart pictures the unbreakable seal of the Spirit, and love that cannot be bought shows God's grace is unmerited, not purchased by works.
teachings.text:
We are in the final chapter of the Song of Solomon, and the opening verses are the woman, longing to openly display affection for her beloved, the way a sister and brother as family could, without being despised. Without the judgment that would come for a maiden to kiss and embrace a lover, even betrothed, in public.

We seem to have come full circle to the beginning of the song. The wedding hasn't happened, the separation and then regained relationship. It is as if she's been dreaming the experience from courtship to maturity, as told in chapters 2-7.

There are repeated stanzas, ideas and the chorus again in verse 4;

 *I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, until he please.*

The longing to be with him, and to experience his love, to be in his embrace, echos her plaintive desires in the first few chapters.

But here, after charging the daughters of Jerusalem again, they sing;

*Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved?*

They see the love-changed woman, who was the girl they had watched grow.

The woman professes her love;

*Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm: for love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave: the coals thereof are coals of fire, which hath a most vehement flame.*

The eternal and unbreakable seal of the Spirit, set upon our hearts, once we know Him and are known of Him.

The love of Christ is like an unquenchable fire, the floods cannot drown it. Noah found grace in the eyes of God. His love for man endured, despite *the* flood.

The love of God could not be purchased, even if a rich man sold all his substance for love, he would be despised. It is not found in riches and cannot be bought by our works. It is unmerited. Freely given.

The woman's brothers join the choir, seeing their sister still as the immature girl they have known. Wondering what they shall do for her now, at her betrothal. A reality that big brothers and parents face, when their daughter has matured.

They contemplate what they'd do metaphorically, if she were a foundational wall or a door in need of a frame. But she states that she is fully grown. She is a wall and the breasts of her maturity are towers. An allegory for the maturity to come to the Lord, and find His grace.

teachings.title: All scripture, even Proverbs, is about Christ
teachings.summary: Proverbs carries the gospel that none is righteous, and all scripture including Proverbs is about Christ the Word, through which faith comes by hearing.
teachings.text:
*Most men will proclaim every one his own goodness: but a faithful man who can find?*

There is none righteous, no not one.

*Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?*

As we have seen, the gospel message, the understanding that we are all sinners, that God has made provision for us in His grace, is found throughout the book of Proverbs. Is there any great wisdom? Is there any more perfect truth?

We are constantly instructed to walk in the way of the Lord and to seek after truth. The word of God being a light unto our feet. Jesus Christ IS *the* way, *the* truth and *the* light. He is the Word of God made flesh. To whom all the prophets gave witness. The promise made to man throughout history.

God's word is the Word. All scripture, given by inspiration, is the word of God and all scripture, including the Proverbs of Solomon, are the word, and all are about Christ.

*Mercy and truth preserve the king: and his throne is upholden by mercy.* So there is no wonder that the Bible says;

Psalm 45:6 *Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a right sceptre.*

The infinite mercy and perfect truth make establishes the fact that His throne is forever.

*Man's goings are of the Lord; how can a man then understand his own way?* The Lord calls all men to His way, to follow Him on the path of righteousness, and He uses His word to do so.

*The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, the Lord hath made even both of them.*

Because;
**Romans 10:17**
*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God*.

But those that are dull of hearing, who haven't the eyes to see, remain lost.

**Matthew 13:15-17** 
*For this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them. But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear. For verily I say unto you, That many prophets and righteous men have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them; and to hear those things which ye hear, and have not heard them.*

As Lord, we see the wicked scatter from His gaze, because He brings the wheel over them. We are told, "vengeance is mine, sayeth the Lord," or;

*Say not thou, I will recompense evil; but wait on the Lord, and he shall save thee*

He shall save thee, from all evil. God values true weights and measures, the balances of trade, because He judges with perfect righteousness. Weighing every man. Just so, having an unjust balance is an abomination to Him.

The wisdom of Proverbs isn't only found in the daily application. The understanding that a man of integrity is blessed and his children as blessed after him. A good reputation from honesty is an inheritance. (And a warning that an inheritance can be squandered). Therefore a child isn't only judged by their father;

*Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work be pure, and whether it be right.*

But more than this practical advice, we actually are given a glimpse into the mind of God. To see things as He sees them. That we may walk in His ways and live! Is there anything more valuable?

*There is gold, and a multitude of rubies: but the lips of knowledge are a precious jewel.*

teachings.title: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination
teachings.summary: God hears the prayer of the upright but the wicked's show of piety and self-made sacrifices are an abomination, since they go about to establish their own righteousness instead of submitting to God's.
teachings.text:
The constant reminder from God to heed the wisdom of your father, to incline your ear to instruction, to prudently regard reproof continues to be hammered home.

Following after the way of righteousness is wise, but those that have forsaken the way of God despise correction and hate reproof. Scorners hate being reproved of their ignorance. They won't seek after the wise. They feed on foolishness, are destitute of wisdom, their plans come to naught for lack of counsel, those greedy of gain and their pride brings destruction to their house.

*The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the Lord: but the prayer of the upright is his delight.*

*The Lord is far from the wicked: but he heareth the prayer of the righteous.*

Having God on your side, accepting your prayers, working in your life is a treasure beyond measure. The wicked and their public display of piety, their self-righteous works and so-called fasts, the "sacrifices" they make, be it the Old Testament animal offerings, or the vows made today to "cut out sweets," or to "drink less" or whatever, are an abomination to the Lord.

*The fear of the Lord is the instruction of wisdom; and before honour is humility*. The wicked may have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge. They lack the humility that comes before wisdom.

**Romans 10:3**
*For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God.*

The humility of submitting to His righteousness, the fear of the Lord, that we may gain understanding, being willing to receive reproof and correction, to seek after knowledge and study to be approved before God, that we may have a ready answer to all for our hope, this is the wisdom and the way we must seek.

*The way of life is above to the wise, that he may depart from hell beneath.*

teachings.title: The root of the righteous shall not be moved
teachings.summary: Proverbs carries a consistent gospel message: a man is made good by faith that comes by the word, and the root of righteousness is Christ, not Israel as dispensationalists claim nor Peter as Catholics claim.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 12** opens with another reminder that loving instruction and knowledge is precious, and the way of righteousness, while hating correction and wisdom is brutish and wicked.

And verse two reiterates that a good man - the just, wise, fearful of God who seeks after knowledge and walks in His ways, obtains favor from the Lord, but the wicked are condemned.

**Proverbs 9:10**
*The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding*.

**Hebrews 11:6**
*But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.*

**Romans 10:17**
*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*

**Romans 5:1-2**
*Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ: By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God.*

**Ephesians 2:8**
*For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God*...

We see how a man is made good, by the fear of God and hearing of His word, by faith seeking Him and truth, and by faith we have access to His grace, we obtain the favor of the Lord, receiving His gift of salvation.

The consistent gospel message of Proverbs cannot be overlooked.

Wickedness cannot establish a man, but the root of Righteousness, that is Christ Jesus, shall not be moved. He is the "root of Jesse" and a "branch of righteousness" (**Isaiah 11, Jeremiah 23:5-6**), established as the foundational righteousness for all believers. Through faith, believers are grafted into this root, allowing them to bear the fruit of righteousness, by the precious seed of His word.

Romans 11:16-18 
*For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches. And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert grafted in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee.*

Dispensationalists will claim the root is Israel, but it has always been Christ. Just as Catholics will claim Peter, "a stone," is the rock, which actually is the profession that Jesus is Christ. Because no other foundation can be laid;

**1 Corinthians 3:11**
*For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.*

All wisdom leads to Christ.

**Matthew 7:24-25** 
*Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.*

teachings.title: Like Job, our end better than our beginning
teachings.summary: Like Job, believers pass through trials from the Accuser, but by grace through faith our end at the adoption and resurrection will be glorious, joint heirs with Christ.
teachings.text:
A reflection on **Job** and his later end being better than his first, and the salvation of his (and our) Redeemer:

Like Job, we are born of woman and blessed by God to an abundant life, no matter our station, having life. When temptation comes, and the law enters, and sin slays us, the Accuser, Satan, does his worst to us (tempered by God's mercy).

We have trials, and tribulations. But, entering into grace by faith, we have the hope and promise of God in Christ that our end will be better than our beginning. That at the adoption, when we put on immortality and shed corruption, when we are redeemed, our end will be glorious, as we will be like Him. And like Lot's children, male or female, we are made joint heirs with Christ.

teachings.title: Seeing Christ in Job is no anachronism
teachings.summary: The Old Testament is all about Christ, so Job's Holy One and Redeemer is Christ and OT saints were saved by the same faith in the same Savior.
teachings.text:
Many argue that Jesus wasn't known in the Old Testament, that salvation by faith didn't exist. That it is an anachronism to see Jesus in Job, and *the Holy One*.

There is no anachronism when we see Christ in in the Old Testament. It is entirely about Him.

He is the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world. The same Word who was with God and was God, Who walked in the furnace with Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.

He was the Rock in the wilderness.

Job’s cry a few chapters from now, “I know that my Redeemer liveth” being about Christ is not an anachronism or a theological reach; it is an inspired revelation.

When Job clings to the Holy One as his strength and hope beyond death, he is laying hold of the same eternal Christ who is the substance of every shadow, the end of every type, the answer to every promise.

The Old Testament saints were saved by the same faith, looking to the same Savior, the same redemption, if through a veil that has now been torn.

teachings.title: Job: faith in God before Abraham
teachings.summary: Job shows that men feared and called on the Lord before and outside Abraham's seed, so salvation by grace through faith was always offered to all people.
teachings.text:
The Book of Job begins with the introduction of a man in the land of Uz, the titular character; Job. Uz, from the biblical clues appears to be a fertile plane in the Arabian peninsula, near where Edom would be. The time frame, many believe, is during the era of the patriarchs; Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

It would be good to note that, Abraham, or Abram, was a Chaldean, a nation who are mentioned here in this chapter located in what is modern Iraq. Where the seat of Babylonian power would be. And he was called out from the city of Ur there, to go unto Hebron by God.

And, as mentioned throughout his story and his sons', there were people in this post flood era who feared the Lord, and offered sacrifices unto him.

Of course we know about Melchizedek, King of Salem, and high priest, and the tenth of the spoils offered by Abram to Melchizedek. Many consider him to be a pre-incarnate appearance of Jesus.

All this to say that the idea of the worship of God originating with Abraham, and only his seed after the flesh, is incorrect. There were many following the flood and the dispersion of nations out from Babel, that called upon the name of the Lord for salvation, and sought to offer the blood as a picture of their faith in Him, as we see Job does for himself and his family.

One of the conceits of modern Zionism and dispensationalism holds that only the sons of Israel after the flesh were special, and that they invented monotheism. But throughout the Bible we find people who were not of that line, and not given to idols and false gods. It's important to understand that salvation has always been by grace alone through faith in the Lord, calling upon his name. And that salvation was always offered to all people.

We will see in Exodus the mixed multitudes that followed Israel into the wilderness from Egypt. We will see high priests of other nations that fear the Lord. There will be people like Ruth and Rahab and others who have the faith.

The distinction for Israel was that they were given the oracles of God. That they had the prophets and the word of God delivered directly to them, and given the law of the Lord that they may be perfect, complete, and a light unto the Gentiles. The other nations. Calling all men to repentance.

But we see the greatest man on Earth at this moment, according to God, who feared Him, eschewing evil, offering sacrifices to sanctify himself and his family. Without the law. Without the temple. Without a priesthood. Without the oracles of God, knowing by the faith of his fathers what was expected.

teachings.title: The Lord rebuke thee: Joshua made clean
teachings.summary: Joshua the high priest made clean without the temple pictures cleansing by grace through faith and points to Christ the Branch and corner stone, while railing against Satan is not God's way.
teachings.text:
**Zechariah 3** presents the prophet with a vision of the high priest Joshua, in the time of Zerubbabel and the restoration of the Temple in Jerusalem. And the angel of the Lord stood before him, and Satan at his right hand to resist him. To accuse him and tempt him.

The Lord rebukes Satan, the adversary, just as in **Jude,** where angels, even archangels, who all are mightier than man, don't bring railing accusations or curses against the Devil, but say "the Lord rebukes thee."

There are many who have built an entire ministry on the basis of "rebuking Satan," railing against the devil. Not resisting him, that he flees, but they themselves speaking evil of dignities, railing against things they don't understand. They often come with a false gospel, adding works or strange doctrines. Charismatics and charlatans.

But the Lord rebukes Satan here, saying that Joshua was an iron plucked from the fire. His instrument. Even as the Lord set His name on Jerusalem, so He had chosen Joshua to be His high priest.

In the vision, Joshua is arrayed in filthy garments. And those that stood before him are ordered to take them away, that the Lord would clothe him in a change of raiment. Making him clean.

Just as Jude writes of saving some by fear, pulling them from the fire, hating even the garments spotted by the flesh. Just as Jesus promises to clothe those who believe on His name in white.

For the priests of the Old Testament must be cleansed and sanctified, made holy by diverse washings and sacrifices, but Joshua, without the temple and without the purification rituals was made clean by grace through faith by the living God.

Joshua is given a fair mitre, a head covering for the office, and fine garments, as the angel of the Lord stood by.

And again, we are given a conditional promise to the high priest, *Thus saith the Lord of hosts; If thou wilt walk in my ways, and if thou wilt keep my charge, then thou shalt also judge my house, and shalt also keep my courts, and I will give thee places to walk among these that stand by.* The angels around him.

Then he is told through the prophet, that the Lord will bring forth His servant, the Branch, a promise of Christ Jesus. He says He will lay before Joshua a stone, that rock of salvation as Christ is called;

**Isaiah 28:16**
*Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste.*

As in **1 Peter 2:6-9**
*Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded. Unto you therefore which believe he is precious: but unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner, And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed. But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light*

The image of Christ as the foundation, the corner stone, perfect and square, and the sanctification in Him of the royal priesthood, carrying over from the Old Testament, done away with, and given to a new priesthood of believers, washed clean in the blood.

The Lord of hosts says, *I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day. In that day, saith the Lord of hosts, shall ye call every man his neighbour under the vine and under the fig tree.*

That blessed day, at the coming of the Lord of hosts. Amen.

teachings.title: Salvation by faith, national promises by works
teachings.summary: Individual salvation was always by grace through faith, but God's national promises to Israel were conditional on their obedience, and they failed and were cast out.
teachings.text:
While spiritual salvation was always by grace through faith for individuals, without any other conditions, the national promises were always contingent on works.

Separation, sacrifice and ritual cleansing to maintain the presence of the glory of God, which we saw earlier in Ezekiel, went out from the Temple, and here in these prophecies, promised to return, if they got right. And the Law was perfect and glorious to that end. The fault wasn't with that covenant, but with the people.

**Hebrews 8:6-8**
*But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises. For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah*

The moral law and commandments, which are still in effect today in the NT, were a schoolmaster to lead us to Christ for salvation. Same then as today. Even the law written in our hearts, for the Gentiles without the advantage of the oracles of God. All have sinned and fallen short, so we need a spiritual redeemer.

But the laws of sanctification and reconciliation for the physical nation were not only doable, but God gave pretty explicit instructions on how to maintain it, which some of the time -  during the period of the Wilderness, the entry into the promised land, here and there during the time of Judges and Kings, they managed to keep. And had God's blessings upon them.

Israel was meant to be a light unto the world. Showing all nations that if they did these things and sought after God, they would be blessed as well. Eventually, it would lead to the culmination of the time of Christ, the BRANCH, The Lord, the King of Kings, coming to establish all of the end times promises of the Kingdom given to the people. In the city He chose to place His name. In the line of David as promised.

And they would not.

So, when Jesus did come, the leaders of the Jews were unable to deliver a people meet for repentance. They, being teachers of the Law were blind guides, thinking that whatever promises they had, were deserved being "Abraham's seed." That their added rituals and Pharisaical cleansings meant they deserved both the spiritual salvation and the restoration of their earthly kingdom.

And rather than being ready for the Kingdom, they were instead cut off and cast out.

**Matthew 8:11-12**
*And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven. But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.*

teachings.title: Preaching Christ from Micah
teachings.summary: Christ could be preached from Micah as Philip preached from Isaiah 53, since the Old Testament is entirely about Jesus and salvation has always been by faith.
teachings.text:
Continuing a thought from the study of Hosea; Christ could be preached to unbelievers through the book of Micah, just as Jesus was preached to the Ethiopian Eunuch by Phillip, using **Isaiah 53**. Micah, like the other prophets, preached judgment for sin, the holiness of God, the truth of His mercy and His Messiah, and redemption by faith in His word, and a call to sanctification and separation for us once saved.

We are blessed to have the clear Gospels, but you can see how there were always a righteous remnant. 7,000 who hadn't bowed the knee to Baal. How the Old Testament was entirely about Jesus and salvation has always been by faith, calling upon the name of the Lord.

teachings.title: Repent ye: John the Baptist's call to believe
teachings.summary: Repent means to change your mind and believe, not to stop sinning, so those John baptized confessing their sins had believed and were saved, baptism being the answer of a good conscience, not its cause.
teachings.text:
Repentance Moment:
**Matthew 3:1-12**
*In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea, And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight. And the same John had his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey. Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judaea, and all the region round about Jordan, And were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins. But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?*
*Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance: And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham. And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: therefore every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire. I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance. but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.*

Repent ye; for the Kingdom of heaven is at hand.

Repent means to change your mind, to accept new information as true and have a change of heart, a conversion.

Here, John the Baptist is saying "Reconsider what you know and believe me." He is not saying "get your life together and stop sinning, the Kingdom of Heaven is here." They were baptized in the water confessing their sins, because they believed him, and were saved.

While false gospels that add works to salvation may disagree, Bible believing Christians who know water baptism is an answer for a good conscience before God, and not the cause of it, should be able to understand this context.

John further chastened the religious leaders of the Jews, who came down to see him and his work, making the paths straight for the Lord. He asks them who has warned them to flee the wrath to come? Where are their followers come to be baptized before the coming of Christ? Where is their fruit meet for repentance? If they had preached the coming of Christ, they would have followers ready to accept the truth that the Christ was come. But this generation of vipers did not. They were trusting in being seed of Abraham.

The water baptism of repentance, the sign of believers, was a prelude for the baptism of the Spirit in Christ. A baptism of fire. Amen

teachings.title: To obey is better than sacrifice
teachings.summary: False religion offers its own righteousness and costly works instead of believing on Christ's righteousness, which God calls rebellion and witchcraft.
teachings.text:
*Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.*

This is so hard for people trapped in false religion to grasp. They believe their own righteousness must be offered in sacrifice, even if it means going against the command of God to believe on His Son's righteousness instead.

They will dress it up as Saul did. That they are offering the best. Buildings made of marble and images laid with gold, and sacrifices made to idols representing, in their minds, Christ. Doing all these works that they reasoned for themselves as good. That their logic of men and vain traditions came up with, often through compromise and fear of the people.

God despises it. It is witchcraft. Rebellion.

teachings.title: The true purpose of God's commandments
teachings.summary: Beyond being a schoolmaster and for the lawless, the law's real purpose is to show the saved God's will for a successful life, not to earn salvation.
teachings.text:
*Only be thou strong and very courageous, that thou mayest observe to do according to all the law, which Moses my servant commanded thee: turn not from it to the right hand or to the left, that thou mayest prosper withersoever thou goest. This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success. Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.*

This is the true purpose of God's commandments. This is how the law is relevant to those saved by the law of liberty, by grace through faith in Christ Jesus.

Yes the law is a schoolmaster that brings us to understand we need salvation. Yes the law of for the lawless, that they may be punished according to the will and perfect judgement of God.

But it's real purpose is for a righteous people to know the will of God for their lives, and in keeping it as best they can, have a prosperous and successful life in service to our God.

Those that make this obedience to the law their gospel, and seek to work their own righteousness as a means of achieving or maintaining their salvation, miss the point and whatever gain they receive is offset by their constant doubts and fears. Not having faith, they please not God. Their filthy rags of their own righteousness give them nothing but hopelessness.

This isn't a prosperity gospel. There is no promise of riches and earthly wealth. But true success in our walk with Christ. Being taken care of, all we need, that we may store up riches in heaven. That we may be saved and all our house. That we may win souls and edify the brethren.

Amen

teachings.title: Meditate therein day and night
teachings.summary: As with Joshua, believers are saved by faith and blessed in this life by loving and keeping God's word, so be strong and not afraid.
teachings.text:
Beginning the **Book of Joshua**, the narrative of the capture of Canaan by the Israelites, the land given them by God for their rest, led by a deliverer named Joshua, a Hebrew variation of the name Jesus. A picture of the Christ to come.

We read the Lord speaking to Joshua as He had Moses, and reaffirming the promises made in His word, upon which Joshua trusted. By faith the people would possess the land for an inheritance, which God had sworn unto their fathers. The Lord's promise is the same to those of us who believe;

*I will not fail thee, nor forsake thee*.

The captains of the tribes give their loyalty to Joshua, to lead them in Moses' place. And God reminds Joshua of the promise made in the covenant with Moses, that if they obey His commandments, and follow His law, turning neither to the right nor the left, that they shall prosper. That by meditating day and night upon His word, and letting His law depart not from their mouth, they will have good success.

This promise is to us as well. That if we love His word and keep it in our hearts, His law upon our lips, meditating on it day and night, we will prosper and have success in this life.

Like the Israelites, we are saved by faith, delivered by His mighty hand into the promised land, but we are also blessed in this world by keeping His commandments. That it be well with us. This is the hope of God, the good news of His Gospel. The same faith that saves us today, and the same obedience that blessed those who keep His law. So be not afraid.

*Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.*

Amen

teachings.title: Repent of sins teachers are least forgiving
teachings.summary: He observes that churches teaching repentance of sin as a condition of salvation become self-righteous and unforgiving, having lost grace and humility.
teachings.text:
As an aside, in my experience, churches and people who teach repentance of sin as a condition of salvation tend to be the least forgiving.

They take pride and hope in their own righteousness, and need to compare themselves to the sins of others so that they can make themselves feel holier. This is the sin of self-righteousness. Something that used to be widely understood in Christian circles. But with the rise of things like lordship salvation and repent of your sins heresy that grace and mercy and humility has gone out the window in many congregations today. They become respecters of persons. They give themselves some credit for being freed from bondage in Egypt rather than understanding, it was by the grace and mercy of God.

Something to keep in mind

teachings.title: Release of debts a picture of salvation
teachings.summary: The release of servants and debts in the seventh year pictures salvation in Christ, so we should forgive debts as God forgave ours and send others away blessed.
teachings.text:
I covered the law of jubilee before, in [Leviticus 25](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/11512). It is worth noting again that the redemption of the servant and the forgiveness of debts, like the Hebrews being freed from bondage in Egypt, are pictures of the salvation found in Christ Jesus. We are called upon to release people of their obligation to us, in time. That if they haven't paid us back by the 7th year, to forgive them their debt, as God has forgiven ours.

*And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt, and the Lord thy God redeemed thee: therefore I command thee this thing to day.*

And as a servant, not just sent away at the end of the term, but sent away with blessings and furnished to succeed on their own. Not as you took them in, but *wherewith the Lord thy God hath blessed thee thou shalt give unto him.*

Just as God does every believer.

Think not too highly of yourself. Remember your fallen state. Remember that God has sealed you as the servant who will not leave your side. As the pierced ear signified here in the law. We are sealed by the Spirit, to be His servants forever.

teachings.title: Why the law cannot save
teachings.summary: Keeping God's law is for our good but not for salvation, since no one can keep it all; the law is a schoolmaster bringing us to Christ to be justified freely by grace through faith.
teachings.text:
We should also remember that obedience to the civil laws of God are for our benefit. For our good always. That it be well with us. That it prolongs our days and that we are preserved alive. Not for salvation. Not for our own righteousness.

The law is a schoolmaster, teaching us our need for salvation in Christ.

**Galatians 3:24-27**
*Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith. But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster. For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus. For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.*

Because;

I*t shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.*

If we observed to do **all** these commandments, it would be our righteousness. We would have to glory.

**Romans 4:1-12**
*What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found? For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God. For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness. Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt. But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, And whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin. Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness. How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision. And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also: and the father of circumcision to them who are not of the circumcision only, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which he had being yet uncircumcised.*

But knowing that it is impossible in our flesh to observe all these things, we understand that it is God's glory that His mercy is revealed.

**James 2:10**
*For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.*

**Romans 3:10-12**
*As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God.*
*They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.*

As Paul writes a few verses later, *There is no fear of God before their eyes.* But as Moses writes here in **Deuteronomy 6**, under the same Spirit as Paul, we are to learn the law of God and keep it in our hearts, in our minds, *That thou mightest fear the Lord thy God*.

And in that fear, that respect and love of the Lord, we may know we have His mercy towards us:

**Romans 3:23-26**
*For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.*

teachings.title: Remember thou wast a servant in Egypt
teachings.summary: Remembering we were servants to sin freed only by grace, believers should show the same mercy to others, even strangers, that they may come to Christ.
teachings.text:
*And remember that thou wast a servant in the land of Egypt, and that the Lord thy God brought thee out thence through a mighty hand and by a stretched out arm: therefore the Lord thy God commanded thee to keep the sabbath day.*

The spiritual application of this understanding, that Jesus is the Sabbath, that our works contribute nothing to our salvation should be coupled with remembering that we were servants to sin. That we were in bondage in Egypt. That before God brought us out from the ministry of death and into eternal life by His mighty hand, we were as slaves, just as the Hebrews were.

And the extension of the Sabbath to those who are our sons and daughters, our employees, and even to strangers, is to show the same mercy given us who were once servants, that they may come to know the truth in Christ.

Never forget that we were servants in Egypt, and only are free by the grace of the Lord. Have charitable love for the unsaved that they may be lifted out of bondage as well.

teachings.title: The Passover open to every stranger
teachings.summary: The Passover pictures salvation in Christ offered to anyone, the unclean and the stranger alike, with those who refuse cut off, and after salvation we follow the Lord.
teachings.text:
We are in **Numbers 9**, and we see this the 3rd Passover, held in the wilderness and the Lord tells Moses not to forget the ordinance that He has established, using the Passover in Egypt and the physical salvation of Israel as a picture of Christ and the individual salvation of man. I've done larger studies on the parallels and processes [before](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/9752). But it is always good to note that it was a reminder of Christ to come, just as the Lord's supper is a reminder of Christ for us now.

Here, God provides Moses with a few guidelines given circumstance. That the ceremonially unclean and those sojourning participate in Passover just the same, that strangers among them that wish to are invited, and those that don't participate are cut off and bear their own sin.

The parallels are pretty clear as to how this corresponds to individual salvation in Jesus. Anyone. Even the unclean. Even those afar off from God, get to participate in the sacrifice and the blood. Even the stranger among them. The sinner, the worldly, the Gentile...all are invited to take part in the salvation by the blood, in the faith of Jesus Christ.

And those who don't are cut off and made to pay for their sin.

It is that simple. People try to overcomplicate salvation because they want to make it about themselves or to make it a sensual experience that they can "feel," or see. Because they lack faith, which is the evidence of things unseen.

And then we are called to follow Him.

Just as the movement of the Tabernacle and the camps was dictated by the movement of God upon them, the pillars of smoke and fire. At the commandment of the Lord they moved. At His command they rested.

And so it is to be in our lives, that after salvation we follow the Lord.

teachings.title: The redemption of the firstborn
teachings.summary: The shekels paid for the firstborn beyond the number of Levites picture the price of our redemption, paid by Christ, God's firstborn Son.
teachings.text:
God's original plan for the children of Israel was that their firstborn sons would be given to Him in service to the Lord, and the firstborn cattle as sacrifice, thus a picture of Christ Jesus. But the children of Israel failed almost immediately after being led from Egypt, worshipping the golden calf;

**Exodus 32:25-29**
*And when Moses saw that the people were naked; (for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies:) Then Moses stood in the gate of the camp, and said, Who is on the Lord's side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him. And he said unto them, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Put every man his sword by his side, and go in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbour. And the children of Levi did according to the word of Moses: and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men. For Moses had said, Consecrate yourselves today to the Lord, even every man upon his son, and upon his brother; that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day.*

This incident changed the plan, and instead a generational priesthood was created from the Levites, under the charge of Aaron.

And so this left an accounting due the Lord.
