Liberated from the fear of death found in transgression of the law by our redemption in His perfect work. Just as the prophets and scriptures promised. Just as those who came before believed on for salvation.

This is the good news. This is the Gospel.

teachings.title: The White Throne Judgment of the Dead
teachings.summary: The great white throne judges the damned blotted out of the book of life, who go to the lake of fire, and only faith in Christ escapes that judgment.
teachings.text:
Here we are given the Millennial Reign in fewer than 15 verses. The binding of Satan in Hell. The saints ruling and reigning the earth in judgment with Christ for that period. Those that sacrificed the most for the cause of Christ given more authority. Until the little season where Satan is given freedom to convince the living humans on earth who resent the rule to rise up against Jesus and the saints. They are destroyed in a moment by fire. Death and then the judgment.

The Great White Throne judgment is of the dead. The damned. Great and small, whose names were blotted out of the Book of Life. Judged by the books of the law, the scriptures of God. His precepts. Written in our hearts, His wrath written in all of creation, that man may have no excuse. And they all have the second death, the lake of fire, the final place of Hell and death, to be tormented for eternity.

Remember, no where in scripture does it say any of one gets written into the Book of Life. It was written before creation, and contains every one that lives. Who are then blotted out if they be reprobate or die without the testimony of Jesus. We can only escape the judgment by faith. Accepting the free gift of salvation given by grace from God.

**Matthew 7**
*21 Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.*

*22 Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?*

*23 And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.*

**John 6:40**
*And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

**Ephesians 2:8-9**
*For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast.*

**Titus 2**:**12-13**
*For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world; Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ*

teachings.title: The Fall Feasts Picture the Second Coming
teachings.summary: The fall feasts of Leviticus 23 picture Christ's second coming, and their commanded rest from all work pictures salvation by grace without works.
teachings.text:
The Levitical feasts are also important to understand for our study of Revelation going forward. They are a picture of Christ. Last Easter I gave a rundown of the ways Jesus fufifiled the spring feasts, Passover, the feast of unleavened bread and Pentecost. These were a picture of His first coming. Likewise, the fall feasts God commands in **Leviticus 23** represent Christ at His second coming. The timing, the harvest, the gathering. The blowing of trumpets. The dwelling in houses made by God, while singing His praises. All point to end times Bible prophecy. ("Booths" were tabernacles, tents, made from branches and boughs, rough cut and gathered from nature). The timing of things mirrors events in Revelation, as we will see.

One incredibly important point of the feasts, these Sabbaths; NO WORK was to be done by the people. This is the reinforcement by God of His grace in giving us a free gift of salvation in Jesus, who is the Sabbath. Three days of no works, 3 Sabbaths in a row, from His crucifixion to His resurrection, Jesus doing all the work. And like the Spring feasts, the convocations or gathering of the congregation/church, there is no work allowed, for Jesus did it all.

*For whatsoever soul it be that shall not be afflicted in that same day, he shall be cut off from among his people.*
*And whatsoever soul it be that doeth any work in that same day, the same soul will I destroy from among his people.*

These are those unsaved who are appointed to wrath. Notice it is both the unbelieving, those not afflicted by the atonement made by the sacrifice, and those who do any work who are cast out and destroyed. So too will it be in the second coming.

We should all be familiar with **Matthew 7:21-23**:
*Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven. Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works? And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.*

**Romans 4:6-8**
*Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin*.

**Psalm 32**
*Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered. Blessed is the man unto whom the Lord imputeth not iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no guile.*

teachings.title: Do ye not hear the law? The bondwoman and the free
teachings.summary: Paul's Hagar-Sarah allegory warns that adding works of the law to faith puts men under bondage, while salvation is God's free gift that cannot be lost.
teachings.text:
And so with this better understanding of the allegory, of recognizing that the entire Old Testament is about Christ Jesus and salvation by faith alone in him, to redeem us, offered by God the father in love and grace, we can understand the righteous anger of Paul writing unto the Galatians.

The Church of the Galatians being swayed by judaizers into accepting another gospel, one of bondage to the law. Whereby they were being told that they must circumcise, keep the days and the months and the dietary laws in the carnal ordinances to be saved. Being dragged back to Hagar, the Bond woman and rejecting Sarah and the son of the promise. Of faith.

And Paul writes, "*O foolish Galatians! who hath bewitched you, that ye should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you?"* The Apostle is angry, he says he fears them. He says that he doubts their salvation, which he had labored with them and questions if it was in vain. Paul saying that only an unsaved person who didn't believe the gospel of Faith he presented them would be susceptible to the judaizers dragging them back under the law and away from the liberty of Christ.

*My little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you,I desire to be present with you now, and to change my voice; for I stand in doubt of you.*

 *Tell me, ye that desire to be under the law, do ye not hear the law?*

*For it is written, that Abraham had two sons, the one by a bondmaid, the other by a freewoman.*

*But he who was of the bondwoman was born after the flesh; but he of the freewoman was by promise.*
*Which things are an allegory: for these are the two covenants.*

He says that he's willing to go through this again with them that they may come to Jesus. That they seeking to be brought back under the law, he says don't you even hear the law? And this is what prompts his use of Sarah and Hagar as an allegory. As a teaching moment taken from scripture that they may understand the difference between salvation by faith alone and the bondage of the law.

This is the same message we can give to those claiming Christ who have added works of the law to the salvation given in the simple Gospel of reconciliation and faith.

These judaizers and those bewitched by them will claim that, "Yes it's by faith alone but you have to do the works of the law to be saved. You have to adhere to our vain traditions. To our carnal ordinances. To our dietary restrictions. You don't expect to just be handed salvation? Do you?"

And so they bring people to be the seed after Hagar, not Sarah. And like Ishmael, they do not receive the inheritance which is given by faith in God's promise, not by heirs according to the law.

Just as Sarah was barren from birth, and brought to old age, it took a miracle of God, visited upon her, to bring her the promise. Not by anything she did, for she was not capable, but in God all things are possible.

This is the lesson. *Do you not hear the law?*

If you're trusting in your own works, if you're sewing your own fig leaves, if you're offering the fruit of your garden, instead of the firstling of the flock, if you're committing adultery with Hagar to produce your salvation, repent. Hear the law.

Salvation is given us by God, in His grace, through His Son, Jesus Christ, killed for our sins, a burnt offering, raised from the dead, that we may be redeemed in faith and sealed by the Holy Spirit unto the day of redemption. A free gift that once accepted cannot be lost. Eternal life. Heir to the Kingdom. Sons of God.

teachings.title: Paul received no gospel from man
teachings.summary: Paul received his gospel by revelation, not from men's traditions, and anyone preaching another gospel of works is accursed.
teachings.text:
Notice, Paul writing to the Galatians in the Spirit, God inspired scripture, says this TWICE. For emphasis.

And what was it he preached to the Galatians?

*For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ. But I certify you, brethren, that the gospel which was preached of me is not after man. For I neither received it of man, neither was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ.*

 *For ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews' religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it:*

*And profited in the Jews' religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers. But when it pleased God, who separated me from my mother's womb, and called me by his grace, To reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the heathen; immediately I conferred not with flesh and blood: Neither went I up to Jerusalem to them which were apostles before me; but I went into Arabia, and returned again unto Damascus. Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and abode with him fifteen days.But other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lord's brother.*

*Now the things which I write unto you, behold, before God, I lie not. Afterwards I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia; And was unknown by face unto the churches of Judaea which were in Christ: But they had heard only, That he which persecuted us in times past now preacheth the faith which once he destroyed. And they glorified God in me.*

Don't miss this, Paul makes it emphatically clear he didn't learn any secret traditions of man from any Apostles. He wasn't told what to say by anyone else. He, knowing the scriptures and having by the grace of God the opportunity for salvation in Jesus, was given all to preach to the heathen.

He explains how, after 14 years the issue of Judaizers and the circumcision brought him to go to Jerusalem and talk to the local church there, run by James BTW, and they agreed to send letters out denouncing the judaizers adding works to salvation, and affirming the Gospel:

*Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.*

This is the Gospel. And ANY MAN bringing any other Gospel, especially of works and rites for salvation, IS ACCURSED.

teachings.title: Enoch walked with God
teachings.summary: Enoch, translated by faith and prophet of Christ's coming, is the example of walking separated and pleasing God, and the patriarchs picture the steps of coming to Christ.
teachings.text:
**And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah: And Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters: And all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years: And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.*

**Hebrews 11:5**
*By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.*

**Jude 1:14-15**
*And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.*

I've read that, when we look at these early patriarchs, we can see the pattern for salvation.

Adam knows God, his creator, and knows his sin. Abel brings the blood of atonement, given in faith for redemption. Seth and Enos, that with the mouth, confession is made, calling upon the name of the Lord. And with Enoch, we have the testimony that he walked with God, that he lived separated, pleasing God.

That each of us goes through these steps when we come to Christ and live for Him. An illustration given by God in His word, through the lives of these men.

But what of Enoch? The seventh from Adam (not to be confused with Cain's son, 3rd from Adam), Enoch was a prophet. A preacher, who gave witness in the Spirit to Christ's victory on the day of the Lord.

We know that by faith, he was transformed, translated that he should not see death.

But this is the promise to all saved by faith in Jesus.

**John 8:51**
 *Verily, verily, I say unto you, If a man keep my saying, he shall never see death.*

So what then? What does scripture mean by saying he was "translated?" That he was not found? Does it mean bodily ascension? Literally taken by God, not just his bodily death?

In **John 3**, Jesus says "*no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven,*" referring to Himself.

What then are we to take from this? Is there a hidden meaning to the story of Enoch? Can we dwell in ancient texts and Jewish fables searching for his fate? Certainly.

Lots of rabbi holes to go down with his story.

But what we can know from scripture is that Enoch walked with God, prophesying of Christ, and was pleasing to God. And draw inspiration to live in accordance to that ourselves, seeking to be similarly pleasing to God. In faith. In the Spirit. Not knowing death.

And that's really all that matters.

teachings.title: Coats of skins: the first promise of Christ
teachings.summary: In Genesis 3 God promises the seed who bruises the serpent's head and covers Adam and Eve with skins by shed blood, a picture of Christ's imputed righteousness.
teachings.text:
So having sinned and fallen, God the Father who loves man, offers the first promise of Christ, while laying out the consequences of bringing sin into the world.

To the devil, that old serpent, *Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.*

I plan on expounding on the seed of the woman/seed of the devil, Revelation 12 and how this promise is fulfilled in Jesus in another post.  But note that the seed who bruises Satan's head, and whom Satan bruises the heel, is Christ.

To Eve, *I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.*

Women know pain and complications of childbirth in ways few creatures in creation can. And their season of fertility, more frequent, and their conceptions, multiplied. And by their nature, they shall desire their husbands will.

This last part deserves its own post as well. Both the meaning and implications of this desire, and how man's failure subverts and damages relationships, twisting this God given inclination in woman. (I would also note modern Bible versions change this verse to have opposite meaning, and how that undermines everything).

And to man, through Adam, we are punished;

*Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field; In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.*

The consequences of sin is death. We return to the ground whereof we were made, after a lifetime of labor to feed ourselves and survive. With the very things of nature we had dominion over, turned against us. Struggle. Death. The wages of sin.

But here, in **Genesis 3**, at the very beginning of mankind as a fallen creature, loved by God, He covers our sins.

 *Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.*

Shedding of blood for the remission of sin. Covered by the righteousness of the lamb, slain before the foundation of the world. God gives them this gift, freely. Of His own handiwork, not ours.

And so we are now, still naked. Still in sin. Our nature, made manifest in Adam, to choose struggle and death over obedience. Unable to cover our shame by our own works, and needing instead the gift of God, the blood of Christ, covered in the spotless coat of the lamb, slain without blemish. Given the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ as a gift from a loving and merciful God.

This is the Gospel. This is the same faith, as received by Adam, and passed on to his descendents, who call upon the name of the Lord to be saved, and becoming sons of God.

 *But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name.*

Amen

teachings.title: The trap of works religion and faithless religion
teachings.summary: Works-based religions keep people trapped in sin by trying to justify themselves, while faithless Sadducee-like religion is equally a trap, and Christ calls men to repent of both.
teachings.text:
The hopelessness in hypocrisy of works-based religions, like much of what is considered modern Christianity. Like what is called Judaism. Like what is the religion of the Pharisees. This is such a snare and a trap, as it keeps people mired in their sin, unable to come to forgiveness while they're in their flesh. Because our flesh, our natural man, our old man willfully sins. It's our nature. And as long as people are trapped in a cycle of trying to justify themselves to God by turning from their sin, or engaging in ceremony and sacrament, denying themselves the healing power of Jesus, they become trapped. This stumbling block and snare keeps so many people from even attempting to get right with God.

And the faithless religion of the sadducees, which denies the power of God, the promise of Heaven, the Resurrection in Christ and forgiveness of sins, is equally a trap.

Many who rationalize their way into atheism, reform theology, Calvinism, the catechism of the Roman Catholic church, or the so-called apostolic traditions of the Orthodox, who don't take a literal view of the Bible while adopting the trappings of it, seeking to become righteous in their own wisdom and knowledge, rather than the wisdom and knowledge of the Lord.

These false ways and spiritual traps are what Jesus came to call sinners to repent of that they may be healed. That their sins be forgiven, that they may sin no more.

teachings.title: The ten virgins and the oil of the Spirit
teachings.summary: The oil is the Holy Spirit and the foolish virgins are professing Christians who never received Him, and none can borrow another's oil once the bridegroom comes.
teachings.text:
Matthew 25 continues the Olivette Discourse between Jesus and His disciples, where in the previous chapter He had laid out much of end times prophecy, and His warning and instruction to be watchful and mindful, like a good servant keeping the house while the Lord was away, so as to not be taken unawares at His return. And so, by way of parable, Jesus expounds on this doctrine.

The first, the parable of the 10 virgins, 5 wise, 5 foolish, awaiting the bridegroom, with their lamps. The 5 wise have lamps filled with oil, the 5 fools never bothered, and caught unawares are shut out of the marriage. And in their pleading the Lord says, "Verily I say unto you, I know you not."

The oil is the Holy Spirit, the lamps, our hearts. The foolish virgins, the unsaved who, knowing full well of the bridegroom's pending return were lazy, slumbering.

At His return, the foolish virgins beg the wise for some of their oil, for shared righteousness, but it is not the wise's to give or share. Each must get their own from Christ. And so, the foolish were locked out in the darkness, wailing.

There are many calling themselves Christian who never received the oil, never accepted the Spirit, and tarried and slept while the master is away. Like the virgins, they may well have lived chaste lives, turning from sin, present in the chambers, but never coming to the truth and repentance to be saved.

They believed they could purchase the oil, and return. Be given another chance. But once the wedding feast starts, it's too late.

teachings.title: Godly sorrow and the Corinthians' repentance
teachings.summary: 2 Corinthians 7 shows already-saved believers repenting of sin after Paul's rebuke, and teaches that godly sorrow can lead to repentance unto salvation while worldly sorrow works death.
teachings.text:
Is there a biblical example of repentance from sin? Of turning from, with fresh information changing ones mind, turning towards the correct action in regards to stopping sinful behavior? Yes.

But it's not regarding getting saved (not directly), but of those who had already believed getting right.

In 1 Corinthians, Paul wrote to the saints in Corinth regarding the open fornication among them, and their taking one another to court for petty disputes, among other things. He ripped into them, that they ought to know better and to repent of it, to think better of it. To come to the realization that it is wrong and hurt their ability to do God's will in sharing the gospel, while they had such sin among them.

And in 2 Corinthians, written a year or so later, Paul tells us by way of praising them, that they had repented of it.

**2 Corinthians 7**

*4 Great is my boldness of speech toward you, great is my glorying of you: I am filled with comfort, I am exceeding joyful in all our tribulation.*

*5 For, when we were come into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we were troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.*

*6 Nevertheless God, that comforteth those that are cast down, comforted us by the coming of Titus;*

*7 And not by his coming only, but by the consolation wherewith he was comforted in you, when he told us your earnest desire, your mourning, your fervent mind toward me; so that I rejoiced the more.*

*8 For though I made you sorry with a letter, I do not repent, though I did repent: for I perceive that the same epistle hath made you sorry, though it were but for a season.*

*9 Now I rejoice, not that ye were made sorry, but that ye sorrowed to repentance: for ye were made sorry after a godly manner, that ye might receive damage by us in nothing.*

*10 For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.*

*11 For behold this selfsame thing, that ye sorrowed after a godly sort, what carefulness it wrought in you, yea, what clearing of yourselves, yea, what indignation, yea, what fear, yea, what vehement desire, yea, what zeal, yea, what revenge! In all things ye have approved yourselves to be clear in this matter.*

*12 Wherefore, though I wrote unto you, I did it not for his cause that had done the wrong, nor for his cause that suffered wrong, but that our care for you in the sight of God might appear unto you.*

*13 Therefore we were comforted in your comfort: yea, and exceedingly the more joyed we for the joy of Titus, because his spirit was refreshed by you all.*

Note in verse 10, Paul is giving us a general rule, that godly sorrow, that is sincerely being sorry at a wrong you've done, leads many to the repentance of belief that is salvation, while the sorrow of this world to death.

In other words, being sorry you were caught, sorry you're in trouble, sorry you're paying a price for it, sorry that God has chastised you, this is worldly sorrow, and in it is death, because it isn't genuine, it's selfish.

Paul says, godly sorrow, truly understanding the harm done to others or to God by our transgressions, can lead to repentance towards salvation, a change of mind that cannot be repented of. Faith in Christ, that cannot be lost once gained. Once saved, always saved.

But to the Corinthians, who had already tasted the good word of God, tasted the heavenly gift, and the powers of the world to come, partakers of the Holy Ghost, as they'd already come to repentance unto salvation. The Bible says, *it is impossible...to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.*

So Paul isn't telling the Corinthians that their turning from the sin he pointed out among them is how they were saved, for they were already, but makes this comment as a part of a larger point, regarding their acceptance of his rebuke.

teachings.title: Trent's anathema on faith alone
teachings.summary: The Council of Trent's curse on justification by faith alone puts the Catholic Church against the Bible, which teaches salvation by grace through faith without works.
teachings.text:
The Council of Trent, on salvation by faith alone:

CANON IX.-If any one saith, that by faith alone the impious is justified; in such wise as to mean, that nothing else is required to co-operate in order to the obtaining the grace of Justification, and that it is not in any way necessary, that he be prepared and disposed by the movement of his own will; let him be anathema

CANON XII.-If any one saith, that justifying faith is nothing else but confidence in the divine mercy which remits sins for Christ’s sake; or, that this confidence alone is that whereby we are justified; let him be anathema.

The Bible is anathema to the Catholic Church. Jesus Christ Himself, and Paul, Peter, James, all heretics and anathema to them.

**John 5:24**
*Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.*

**Romans 11:6**
*And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then is it no more grace: otherwise work is no more work.*

**Romans 3:20**
*Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.*

**Ephesians 2:8**
 *For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God.*

**John 3:16**
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.*

teachings.title: Work out your own salvation is not doubt
teachings.summary: Work out your own salvation does not deny assurance, since Paul in the same epistle is confident God will perform the work He began in them by the gospel.
teachings.text:
Philippians is one of my favorite epistles, for it's clear meaning and beautiful prose. It is easily understood and straightforward doctrine on sanctification and doing works of the Lord.

However many works-based false teachers use the "work out your own salvation with fear and trembling" line to teach that you cannot be assured salvation, and that we must do works to be saved. This out of context understanding is contrary to scripture, even scripture within the same epistle. In chapter 1 Paul says:

*For your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now;*
*Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ: Even as it is meet for me to think this of you all, because I have you in my heart; inasmuch as both in my bonds, and in the defence and confirmation of the gospel, ye all are partakers of my grace.*

He has confidence in them, that they partake in the same grace that saved him. This is only conditioned on their having fellowship in the same Gospel he preached to them, not on their works, and with not doubt that God works in them.

It is another case of reading the whole of scripture and comparing it with itself, saving us from bad doctrine.

teachings.title: One gospel preached by Paul and the apostles
teachings.summary: Galatians and Acts 15 show Paul preached the same faith-alone gospel the apostles agreed on, against the Judaizers then and Hebrew roots and works teachers now.
teachings.text:
The letter to the Galatians regarding the false gospel of works brought to them by judaizers, specifically that they must keep circumcision to be saved, contrary to the gospel of grace Paul had won them with.

Paul in chapter 1 and 2 establishes his bona fides in this, that he preaches the same Gospel the Apostles have, not having learned it from them but the Spirit, and confirming it much later, following the meeting with the elders and the council in Jerusalem, written about in **Acts 15**, which followed a similar incident of judaizers preaching circumcision in Antioch.

If you recall, James, the half brother of Jesus Christ and Peter agreed with Paul that this burden of the carnal ordinances of the law must not be required of the Gentiles, least they frustrate the faith alone Gospel they stand by, that saved them.

*Peter rose up, and said unto them, Men and brethren, ye know how that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe.*
*And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us; And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.*

*Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear? But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they.*

This, in one accord, James agreed; *James answered, saying, Men and brethren, hearken unto me:*

*Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name. And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written, After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up: That the residue of men might seek after the Lord, and all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called, saith the Lord, who doeth all these things. Known unto God are all his works from the beginning of the world.*
*Wherefore my sentence is, that we trouble not them, which from among the Gentiles are turned to God: But that we write unto them, that they abstain from pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from things strangled, and from blood.*

There was an idea that Paul changed the nature of the Gospel, removing works from it, and this is something that persists to this day, especially with very online pseudo-Christians, who are taken in by those adding works to salvation, or worse, Hebrew roots heresy, adding the specific ordinance of circumcision and other physical requirements to the faith. But in Acts, and here in Galatians, for example, we see that there has been one faith preached, consistently and that Paul was approved of by the 'pillars' of the early church, even to the shame of Peter, having been being a respecter of persons regarding the Jews in Antioch, and his repentance before Paul, James and the others in Jerusalem.

teachings.title: Why Paul circumcised Timothy
teachings.summary: Paul refused circumcision for Titus because it was pressed as a condition of salvation, yet circumcised Timothy for access to the Jews, since circumcision is nothing when not made a means of justification.
teachings.text:
There is a lot going on here, in this chapter. Especially on the heels of 15, where we see the pillars of the church in Jerusalem issuing their judgment that Paul go to the Gentiles and their denouncing the adding of works to the faith that saved them. They agree at Paul's behest to write and visit the various churches, warning them against taking on the yoke of bondage to the carnal ordinances of the law, primarily circumcision. This crisis comes about by new Christians, confused in the faith by certain men crept in unawares, seeking to force Gentile Titus to be circumcised as part of salvation. Paul steadfastly refuses understanding the what they were attempting to do would subvert the Gospel, and James and the other apostles agree.

Yet here we see Paul circumcised Timothy, who being half-Gentile, but raised Jewish by his mother, would be hindered by the Jews in the region when giving the Gospel. And as Paul says in 1 Corinthians, in this case *Circumcision is nothing,* because it's not being put forth as a condition of justification before God.

We must look at the epistles to Corinth and especially the Galatians for more understanding, and so I think I will devote time to them today and tomorrow.

teachings.title: If thou believest with all thine heart
teachings.summary: Acts 8:37 gives the order of salvation, believing that Jesus is the Son of God and then baptism, which is why modern versions remove or doubt it.
teachings.text:
Now, after Philip has given him the gospel and shown him, out of the Bible the truth of Jesus Christ, the eunuch asks what hinders him from being baptized in the water the caravan had come to, and Philip answers with pure doctrine;

*If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest.*

*And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.*

This is the Gospel. This is how salvation works. This is the order of things, and baptism is but a public expression of the salvation that came from belief.

And so Acts 8:37 is either removed or footnoted into doubt by all modern perversions of the Bible. The simplicity of the Gospel, that we are saved by our belief in this truth that Jesus is the Son of God, the Christ who saves us by His perfect work, as God promised from the foundation of the world.

The removal or doubt-casting on this verse, the clearest and most explicit example of 1-on-1 soul winning thus far in the New Testament, can only be done for one reason, and to serve one agenda; Satan's.

We see the eunuch saved, baptized and Philip carried away by the Holy Spirit, leaving one of the most powerful men in Ethiopia joyfully proclaiming Jesus Christ.

teachings.title: Born of water is the first birth
teachings.summary: In John 3:5 being born of water means natural birth, as verse 6 explains, not baptism, so baptism is no part of being born again.
teachings.text:
Oh one more point of Doctrine from John 3, there are some who like nicodemus, can't understand scripture and so isolate verse 5, out of context, and claim that baptism is part of being born again. That Jesus is saying we must be born both of water, meaning baptism, as well as the Spirit. As we can tell by looking at the entire chapter in context, that's not what's being said at all. Verse 6 explains verse 5, Jesus is saying that we're being born again, because we've already been born once in the flesh, in the water of our birth. So being born in the spirit is our second birth.

Like all bad doctrine, it requires someone to take an autistically literal interpretation of isolated verses, and are as foolish as Nicodemus saying we'd have to crawl back inside our mother to be born again.

teachings.title: John 1: as many as received him
teachings.summary: John 1 shows Christ lights every man, that the world did not know Him, and that whoever receives Him by believing becomes a son of God, refuting limited atonement and irresistible grace.
teachings.text:
Next, the apostle John introduces us to John the Baptist, the voice crying out in the wilderness bearing witness to Christ.

John the apostle again turns to explain Jesus is the true light which "lighteth *every* man." (RIP limited atonement).

V10 states the matter plainly, the creator has come into the creation and the creation didn't even recognize Him, fallen as we are. Man doesn't recognize Christ (rip irresistible grace)

V11 lays the groundwork for replacement theology. The "chosen people" the Jews don't recognize Christ

V11 is the Gospel itself; the good news. "As many received him..." (that's an indeterminate number, meaning 'all who' (limited atonement BTFO, again), "...to them gave he power to become the sons of God" (the promise made by God), "even to them that believe on his name" (the means of obtaining the aforementioned power to be sons of God; BELIEVING, not works or any other means).

V13 Sons born (you have to be born again to be a son or daughter of God). Not by blood (dispensationalism, ded), not by our fleshly desire (none righteous), not by our works (the will of man) but of God.

V14 is the mystery of Christ made flesh revealed.
V15-17 John the BAPTIST (hint) tells us his ministry has been preaching the coming Christ and salvation by grace, not the law.

When JtB is questioned by the Pharisees he testifies that Jesus is the Christ come in answer to what was taught by all the prophets, the faith that saved OT saints was manifest.

About halfway through one chapter and the doctrines are just boom, boom, boom...

teachings.title: Romans 8: adopted after first believing
teachings.summary: Paul builds the case for conditional election: we are adopted as sons and joint heirs only after believing, and foreknowledge comes before predestination, which Calvinists reverse.
teachings.text:
Paul has for the past 7 chapters laid out the factual, Biblical case for *conditional election,* that **we must believe to be saved,** starting with the testimonial of God in creation, the lack of excuse by the unbelieving, the refusal to accept the knowledge of God of the reprobate, and the surety of our salvation of placing our faith in God's promise.

Here, tying together these themes, he speaks of the carnal mind that the saved still have, exhorting the saved by faith to live in the spirit, not the flesh, because in that righteousness given us is adoption into the promise; we become heirs of Christ, we call out to our Father. In verse 9, he makes it clear that this is a **conditional** state of being. You aren't adopted without first believing.

Then, Paul begins building onto this foundational theme of being adopted as sons in the spirit by explaining how God's foreknowledge that we (the saved) then be used to His purpose. (Note the order of operations in verse 29, calvanists reverse it, and thus get none of it).

The glory of being joint heirs with Christ, in Christ. The hope, which is an earnest expectation for the thing we believe to come (not a long-shot wish as some use the term) being shared with all of creation, waiting for that kingdom to come. That we are blameless to charge by any because we are justified in our faith in Christ. That, in faith, none can stand before us as God gives us all things, according to His will.

Having laid out the first faith and its terms and rewards, Paul is making the case to the saved to understand what their faith has opened them up to, what God's gifts mean to us if we now walk in the spirit, quickened by the Holy Ghost, that all things are for good to us for loving God, if we simply trust further in the word of God, building faith upon faith.
